posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
618 YishunNoticed the pork lard had some skin and wanted to revisit. This time I noticed the carrot cake stall was open and asked if I can order one. Old aunty said “Yes can and won’t take so long.”. I the ordered a $5.50 HKM + $4 ingredients + egg fried into noodles and + 1 sunny side up. Don’t know why but had two yolks. I think it’s quite common for her eggs to have two yolks.  Carrot cake was just superb. Won’t elaborate but I get why the queue is so long and I won’t mind ordering it and wait while I eat something else.  HKM was mild in flavor but since I added eggs and there were so much ingredients, it was quite a healthy meal. The pork lard and skin….plenty of good fats and collagen. I understand why so many people revisit. It’s relatively healthy compared to some others, and it’s quite a big portion. Prawns were huge and firm, and was nicely seasoned. Glad to have this as the last HKM for this lunar new year. I couldn’t finish and had to waste food. Sigh. I made it up by fasting the rest of the day and made it my only meal for the day. 618 Yishun Ring Rd, Singapore 760618
+2

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
This stall needs no introduction. If you don’t know this stall, please leave the group. Anyway, jokes aside. Heard of this legendary stall so many times and decided to come try (first time) since I was in the vicinity. Could literally smell the wok hei when I approached the stall. Confirm ho seh liao. Ordered a $7 portion, pretty decent serving size. Waited about 10 mins.First bite. WOK HEIIIII. Solid. Really love the wok hei and mild umami. Noodles were fried really well and still slightly wet and the gooey zhup was just out of this world. Not sure if they offered pork lard, but their pork slices were thick and chunky. 3 medium to large size prawns were fresh. No sotong though. Chilli was not the typical sambal I like but this was quite ok, spicy and sour, goes quite well with the noodles. Overall, superb plate of noodles for me and superb value for $7. PS. I saw their sign board got opeh leave for takeaway, anyone knows if really have? Didn’t had a chance to ask as they were really busy with dinner service.

posts.author: David Yeo
posts.text:
I must confess, for a HKM aficionado, I have not tried Nam Sing. But definitely not for the lack of trying. Many times I reached Old Airport market only to find them sold out and at other times, the wait was more than 40 min, which prompted me to opt for the other famous brand Yi Ji.This brand has survived since 1960s, and it has a fierce following who defends their style, since it could be their growing up comfort food.So let's be objective. The ingredients were definitely fresh and I found the sotong especially to be very fresh and springy. Chilli to me was disappointing, there is only cut red chilli, and not that of the spicy kind. I hear that's the way the ancients have it, before the advent of belachan and chili padi to the dish.Stock wise not as strong flavored as other well known heavyweights, not so much of prawn umami, instead I can taste they opted for slight seafood umami combined with lots of egg. Overall the dish felt very healthy and not too sinful a delight for a HKM. I can see why this could be a comfort food for many, but it unfortunately doesn't hit strong flavorful notes I would have preferred.@Nam Sing hokkien fried meeOld Airport FC

comments.author: Edwin Ng
comments.text: Nice review. Definitely the similarities. Nam Sing has its own following and I never bothered to go back to try as the wait is just unacceptable to me. If your business is really that good, then the right thing is to expand. If you have the right mindset, there will be someone reliable that you can pass the skills on to as evidenced by those mentioned here like Hai Nan being Nam Sing’s apprentice a long time back. I still prefer the newer generation HKM that moved with times (stronger umami and not excuses not to provide sambal chilli). Cut chilli is something I just don’t like.

posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
The Canteen by Enjoy$15.80++ for the HKM. 2 big prawns but not flavorful or juicy. Slightly dry and tasted like those freshwater big head prawns. Claimed to be possibly the best HKM but not on the top 10 on my list. It’s edible and decent, but really not great. It was overly seasoned and had a strong salty taste but also left a “spicy” aftertaste of an excessively seasoned dish. Had two types of bee hoon similar to Fung Yi but of course nothing near that standard. Sotong was rubbery although there were quite a few. Pork was not very flavorful as it felt like the wrong cut of pork was used. Lard was just standard fare. Chilli looked nice but didn’t have much spice nor flavor. Anyway it was a one off and probably pointless to go back for another visit. Other dishes were all pretty average. If you’re thinking of visiting because of the claim of being the best HKM, consider it as me taking one for the team. But if you’re just bored and want to try all the HKM around then maybe you can add this to your list. 383 Jln Besar, Kam Leng Hotel, Singapore 209001

posts.text:
Ho Ji Fried Hokkien Prawn NoodlesVisited at about 9am. Ordered a $5+$4 ingredients +$1 egg. Wow. I was pretty impressed. Was the best plate so far from Ho Ji. Perfect balance of thin bee hoon to noodles and very well fried with wok hei and texture. Broth is also flavorful enough to balance out the strong wok hei. Plenty of pork lard and I used less than half the chilli as I learnt not to put too much. I’d summarize it as “The most bang for the buck and delicious HKM that’s available before 11am.”.  Keep up the great effort, Roger Ho! 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-39 Mayflower Market & Food Centre, Singapore 560162

posts.text: I finally made it here to 69 FHKM in Bedok and I’m very happy to report that this is really one of the better ones (made it to my personal top 10 favourite). Chilli needs abit more oomph ( prefer youfu, shiok or fungyi chilli) but overall a very good plate. I will definitely return again.

posts.author: Marcus Chen
posts.text:
West Sider visits East Side Feng Yi..As an Ah Jie/ NeighbourWok fan, I came to Feng Yi all the way from the west with high expectations due to the Reputation of Feng Yi.Queue was short 15mins .. ordered 4 X $7 plates for parents and Children.. My impression The Pork Lard is THE BEST out of all my fav HKMs.. Amazing!! It literally pulled extra points for Feng Yi. Reminded me of Sio Bak skin! No obvious Wok Hey like NW or Ah Jie, but Broth was flavourful with Seafood taste.. generous portions of Squid/ Pork Belly and Prawns for $7… Chilli reminded me of the Old School Bukit Batok Blk 155 (Yong Heng predecessor).. those who know will know… All in all a pretty impressive plate… satisfied .. **Mum said the garlic bits were a quite lot .. should have fried the garlic longer to get more fragrance .. but concluded that the Pork Lard was really crazy good..
Jeremy

posts.text: Chia Keng Fried Hokkien Prawn NoodlesDecided to just eat around the area. Ordered $8 version. Plenty of sotong, 4 prawns. Broth is tasty and chilli is quite spicy so do add slowly. Those sensitive to yellow alkaline taste should take note that the ratio is a bit high for noodles and it is not fried for very long hence will have some noodle aftertaste. Overall still a nice plate of wet style of hokkien mee. Do note that Chomp Chomp has just completed the renovation. Starts around 430-5pm and rest days on Tuesday. 20 Kensington Park Rd, #01-02 Chomp Chomp Food Centre, Singapore 557269

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
Always wanted to try this stall which is behind my parent’s house. Today finally had the chance. $6 and $9 options available. Accepts paynow. Overall $6 is pretty worth it. Decent sized portion with 3 large prawns. Also got sotong and pork belly, both of which came in pretty chunky pieces. Taste wise it’s tasty, with sufficient umami and prawny taste. It’s the wet and slurpy type, noodles were cooked just about right. The prawns were peeled, and really big and fresh! Auntie asked if I wanted chilli and pork lard, of course want la, still need to ask meh?  Pork lard was decent, most were still crispy. Goes damn well with each spoonful of noodles. As for the chilli, I’m not really a fan of this type of chilli as I prefer the typical sambal. But I did try and it was slightly spicy and sour, but did not overpower the taste of the dish. It’s an above average plate for me. Would definitely come back again when visiting my parent. Lastly, before you start asking “Where?” Please google the stall name la… or look at the tagged location. p.s. the sign board color and pattern look a bit familiar, see liao like very shiok.  anyone knows if any back story?

I reached at 11:33am, waited about 50 minutes and finally got my FHM at 12:23pm.Even with the long wait, the quality is still excellent. Boss Chuan doesn’t rush or cut corners just to serve faster, every plate is cooked properly. The taste is solid, the ingredients are fresh, the pork lard is super crispy and the sambal belacan packs a fiery punch.  If you’ve got an extra hour to spare, Fung Yi in Tampines or Chuan at Circuit Road is absolutely worth the wait. Lunch at Bao Er Cafe at Holland V today and was honestly quite disappointed with the HKM.

The moment I slid open the glass door and stepped in, the entire café smelled strongly of smoke. It’s not the pleasant kind of smoky aroma you’d associate with wok hei, but rather the burnt food kind of smell.

I proceeded to order a plate of HKM and added noodles for an additional $2. Unfortunately, the dish tasted exactly like how the café smelled. Some might mistake it for wok hei, but to me, it was clearly burnt. The overall dish had a bitter, charred taste. The eggs were visibly blackened, and the gravy was unusually dark in colour. From the flavour, it seemed like the bitterness came from burnt residue or carbonised bits from the wok and I’m suspecting they do not wash and clean the wok in between batches to retain the burnt residues. 

After eating regularly at other HKM such as Bedok 69 HKM, Hainan HKM, and Youfu, I can confidently say I know the difference between proper wok hei and food that is simply burnt. 

That said, the staff were polite and service was pleasant. The tea and kaya toast were good, and the prawns used in the HKM were sweet and fresh. It’s a pity the execution of the noodles overshadowed what could have been a decent dish.

Bedok 69
Best HKM in the East in my opinion. We can agree to disagree but there is no doubt most will only have good things to say about this stall. 

Uncle serves a comforting plate of Hokkien mee with a mild wok hei. The noodles are fried well and nicely braised, slightly moist without being overly wet, and well-coated in the savoury broth.

The prawns (de-veined) and sotong are fresh and naturally sweet, which really lifts the dish. The chilli gives a satisfying kick and pairs well without overpowering the noodles. The lard is fresh, crispy and fragrant. 

This is my $8 + $2 noodles + $1egg plate. A size fit for sharing with 2-3 pax.

posts.author: Alvin Pancakie
posts.text:
Today has been a good day for Hokkien mee for me
I tried two hkm today and it turns out to be great
1. Yi ji fried Hokkien mee @ old airport road
51 Old Airport Rd, #01-102, Singapore 390051
Very good plate of hkm .
They replace Sotong with mock abalone or top shell . Chewy texture or texture very similar to Sotong , I get the purpose but might not agree with it completely . To me Sotong texture and taste when cooked well is hardly replaced by top shell but in this case it beats all the mediocre frozen sotongs out there
Mild Wok but the flavour of the stock is so well balanced . Very comforting to take a slurp at it which I did until I finished it
Chili is a power bomb shell as with any yi ji chili at any branch . Very pungent and very sour and spice hits like a truck that might cause lao Sai and spicy ass hole the next day .
Yi ji might not have been on my top list my this time round looking for something comforting on my off day , but this is the taste profile I wanted . Not too punchy like my own , but provide you with an option to hit yourself with their chili . am pleasantly surprised how well this pairs with it
Umami - 5/10
Pork lard -0/10 cos no pork lard visible and they might just do it in veg oil
Chili - 9/10 , minus one point for being too spicy for me
Noodles -7/.510 - very well cooked but not evenly coated . And they do cook one whole batch at least two woks worth to keep for post heating in stock , plus really lack the breath and kiss from hot wok . Garlic taste don’t pop as much but that could be a plus for a lot of ppl
Prawn stock -7.5/10
Lacks umami , but very well seasoned . Not over seasoned that you don’t taste the prawn broth but not overly sweet that it becomes not a savoury dish . Very well done overall
Portion size - 9/10
More than enough for me and comes with three prawns and a good portion of scrambled eggs in the noodles . Portion I had was $5 , super valued .
2. Ah Yu fried Hokkien mee @ East Coast lagoon
1220 ECP, #01-36, stall 36, Singapore 468960
Backstory : Worked in finance and started hkm stall four months ago . Used to work in one of the hkm stall at Fengshan .
Am very impressed with the prawn stock and frying and end product is good .
Umami : 7.5/10
Good umami from prawn heads and pork bone stock . No extra ingredients . Pure prawn stock but would need to work on extracting those flavors more
Pork Lard : 8/10 Crispy no off taste . Very well done
Noodles : 8.5/10 Noodles are fried fresh on the spot . No pre cook noodles , every batch is freshly cooked . Wok taste is mild but noodles are al dente .
Prawn stock : 8/10 , lacking in seasoning but tasted very balanced . No flavours popped but . Not that is a bad thing but I do appreciate it as a comforting plate of Hokkien mee especially when everyone is trying to achieve that edge on wok hei and prawn taste .
Portion size : 9/10
Comes with 2 prawns at $6 , I can’t finish cos portion too big for mee

posts.author: Micheal Chiang
posts.text:
Simple food done right. The fried hokkien mee here is really satisfying with a nice wok aroma and a good balance of yellow noodles and bee hoon. The noodles are moist and flavourful without being overly oily. The seafood adds a natural sweetness and the sour based chilli on the side gives it a great spicy kick.
The fried egg on top is a perfect touch. Breaking the runny yolk into the noodles makes the whole dish richer and more comforting.
Portion is generous and the taste reminds me of classic local hawker style cooking. A very enjoyable plate of noodles that I would happily come back for again.
Address: Bugis Fish Head Steamboat

posts.author: David Yeo
posts.text:
My quest for completing all legendary HKM in Singapore is soon drawing to a close, I do have a few in mind yet to try, and today it brought me to Kelantan Lane.
The stall is primarily a tze char stall, HKM is one of its many dishes, whilst I was staring at the menu looking to order, the stall assistant confidently prompted me "Hokkien Mee correct?". So I guessed they definitely have a steady following of HKM customers. 
The HKM has a surprisingly nice wok hey upon your first mouth, ingredients were plentiful, special mention to the thin sliced fatty pork and crunchy pork lard. One of the best, the pork lard pieces were huge, some of which looked like mini fries! There's sotong, gu chye, tangy chilli and garlic all well proportioned and balanced into every bite. 
The broth was sufficiently reduced and noodle beehoon ratio well maintained. Everything I tasted tells me this chef cooks up a storm of a HKM. 
I rate this alongside Chuan, Ah Ong, Fung Yi. In fact, I think I would make another trip here next time to try their tze char dishes. 
@ Bugis Fish Head Steamboat

I always try to avoid peak hours since the waiting time at Chuan can get overwhelming. Instead, I went around 2pm when the crowd was smaller and enjoyed my lunch. A friend asked me, since I know the bosses, why I didn’t ask to skip the queue. I explained that it would be unfair to their regulars. If everyone expected special treatment, then occasional visitors like me might end up waiting even longer than if we simply followed the queue system. Hawkers already work under immense pressure, so let’s not add to it. Be patient, respect the process, and let them cook in peace. 
Address: Block 80 Circuit Road, #02-05, Singapore 370080

The Neighbourwok @ Bukit Batok is absolutely the best Hokkien mee I’ve had and believe me, I’ve tried almost all the highly popular ones already. The noodles are perfectly moist, infused with strong wok hei and coated in a rich, umami prawn broth. Fresh, juicy prawns and tender squid add sweetness, while crispy pork lard and sambal give it a satisfying punch. Truly comforting, delicious and second to none! My only wish is for them to open an outlet in the East that’s 100% authentic and replicate the awesome taste of the existing stall so that I don’t have to travel 30km to get my HKM fixed which I have been doing it for more than 10x!

posts.author: Gopalsamy Rajkumar
posts.text:
Their portions are noticeably larger than most, offering great value for money with very fresh prawns and sotong. Ingredients are generous and they serve one of the best pork lard in Singapore. For those unfamiliar, 618 Hokkien Mee was the first to introduce sunny-side-up, a trend many other stalls later followed.  
Taste is subjective, but this is one stall I truly enjoy. Whenever I’m here, I always add extra prawns because theirs are big, sweet, and satisfying. Honestly, I hope they don’t get too famous. I’ve experienced the crazy waiting times before and I’d rather not go through that again. These days, a 30nminute wait feels just right.

posts.author: Nicholas Lee
posts.text:
Finally made a trip to the legendary Swee Guan Fried Hokkien Mee, a place that every serious HKM lover has probably visited at least once. Came all the way from the North and managed to get a seat quickly before the queue started forming. I placed my order right away..
Surprisingly, the aunty’s attitude was actually quite pleasant, very different from what many reviews had mentioned.
After about a 20 minute wait, the plate arrived. The wok hei was probably the strongest I’ve experienced from all the HKM I’ve tried so far. It was so intense that it slightly overpowered the umami from the prawn stock. That said, the egg soaked in the prawn stock and combined with the wok hei was easily the highlight of the dish for me.
I left feeling satisfied, not because it was the best HKM I’ve ever had, but because I finally got to try the legendary charcoal fried HKM.
For now, based on my personal list, Chuan and Bugis Fish Head are still at the top of the chart.
Jeremy

comments.text: Between Swee Guan and his late brother, Alex, boss of Geylang Lor 29 fkhm at east coast rd (nw relocated to siglap but no longer great), Alex's fhkm was tastier. posts.author: Takeda Bushido
posts.text:
In life, it isn't always sunshine and rainbow 
. But over here at rainbow rice house I can see the "rainbow". Boss Louis always treats his regulars/customers with warm hospitality and it is not difficult to tell why the hkm is one of the prominent stars in their extensive menu.
Boss Louis has over 20+ years of experience in F&B and his frying skills still maintain tip top over the years. Not just that, he is very open in listening to customer feedback and makes huge improvements on his hkm. The prawn stock is fully infused into the noodles, the sotong, pork belly slices and prawns all are fresh. The chilli can be a tad overwhelmingly spicy for those that can't take the heat. Definitely, one of the best hkm in the CBD area.
I forgot to take the prawn paste chicken side dish as we were too busy wolfing down on the hkm. Highly recommended to come down and try the hkm before boss Louis retires in the future!

Saw this near my place recently and finally today had the chance to try it. No signboard Hokkien Mee haha.. right smack in the heart of Hougang Central at the coffeeshop facing the entrance to Hougang Mall.
$6 a plate, decent size with 2 big prawns, chunky pork belly and sotong. Seafood was really fresh and cooked perfectly! A plus point. This is one of the rare stalls which uses 3 types of noodles (Mee, and both Thin and Thick bee hoon). Noodles are slightly wet style. Wok hei and umami on the mild side, but still quite tasty. Pork lard was decent, slightly “Lao Hong”. The chilli was not to my liking though. Thought it was the typical sambal as per the menu photo, but turns out to be bright red belachan which is fiery spicy. A bit too spicy for me in fact. 
Overall, an average plate for me. Filling for $6, but could improve on the umami flavor. If you’re in Hougang Central can give them a try. They also serve the “Din Tai Fung” style fried rice.

posts.author: Arnold Neo
posts.text:
Something other than the quality of the HKM
Location: Beauty World Shiok HKM
First, pardon the picture of the half-eaten HKM. Couldn't wait to dig in.
Warning: Long post ahead
I'll get the elephant out of the room. The quality of the HKM was good. But rather than the noodles, I'll like to share another observation of the place
The time was 12:30PM, and the lunch crowd was at its full force. It's a warm day, and the orders were coming in fast and furious. All 3 staff were up to their neck trying to fulfill the orders. I trust that you can imagine the kind of environment that we are in
Amidst the chaotic rush, the staff's attitude remained customer-oriented. I was asked politely to wait for a couple of minutes before my order was taken, so that they can clear out the ready plates to the other customers. During ordering, I was informed that the wait could take up to 30 minutes. When I picked up the order, the thank from them was cheery. Even when I asked for lard, they were enthusiastic to offer them to me.
Kudos to the 3 young staff who continued to deliver solid customer service, even though the atmosphere could be frustrating to them.
While the food was good, it's the wonderful attitude from them that made the food taste better than good, making it great!
Keep it up!
Jeremy

posts.author: Meishan Bee Zhu
posts.text:
Had an errand to the east today and Fung Yi is closed. So decided to try 69 Bedok South after reading some reviews here. 
First thoughts: their system is a little chaotic. There was uncle frying in the back. Auntie took my order and went to prep the ingredients for each order. Young man there is responsible for giving out the plates but there was a lot of shouting to confirm which one is for whom. Then when it came to payment, because I used CDC voucher, another uncle suddenly came out of thin air with his phone. 
When I got my order it was a bit messy, cos auntie emerged to confirm these were my orders and the young man stepped away so only 1 plate had chilli. While I was getting my cutlery auntie threw some pork lard in and then told me where I can get chilli for the other plate. And then I realized only after all that, that they forgot the limes entirely. 
But anyway, taste. 
This is $6 (the cheapest) with extra $2 ingredients. 
The pluses: I liked that the prawns were quite firm and cleaned! Nicely deveined. The pork slices are a bit wider than the usual strips. Sotong also cleaned and quite chunky. The pork lard was crunchy and had good flavour. 
The cons: I didn’t like the chilli. Very watery, quite spicy and very sour. However they also sell fish soup so I helped myself to the fresh cut chilli padi. Also they used thick beehoon and my preference is thin, and it seemed a bit heavy on the beehoon ratio.  The prawn flavour wasn’t very pronounced.
Overall the flavour was quite mild. Not unpleasant but lacking the seafood porky flavour that I associate with fried Hokkien mee. Also this is not the wokhei style. 
I went for a late lunch. Got there around 1.30pm. There were a few people waiting for their orders. Like I said no real system. Needed auntie to identify which orders are for whom. But the noodles were already fried and was just finishing with the ingredients. The coffee shop was not crowded and most people were eating from this stall. 
I probably won’t go out of my way to come here. If I’m in the east I’ll just go to Fung Yi Delights 豐億

Jackson Fried Hokkien Mee
Arrived slightly before opening at 12 noon. Ordered a small ($5). Added $3 prawns, $3 oysters, and $1 egg. Total $12. Waited about 15 mins.
Prawns were huge and crunchy but I understand that today’s prawns are not the usual wild caught sea prawns but they were big and firm. $3 got me 3 more than the usual 2 prawns. 8 oysters and although frozen, they were pretty fresh and highly recommended for those who eat oysters as it went very well with the noodles. Slurpy goodness and reminds me of Ah Jie but not as sweet and less wok hei, but made up with more premium ingredients and a generous portion. A few strips of tender sotong and pork belly has the right amount / layers of fat.
I noticed the crowd slowed down at 1pm so either be there at 12pm opening or 1pm and after. Definitely worth a visit if you haven’t tried Jackson. Think they close at 7pm.

posts.author: Takeda Bushido
posts.text:
I think other than the slightly ignorable bean sprout taste, this is one of the most perfect hkm I've ever ate. Rare big swa lors like these are really hard to find in hkms nowadays. When I see such fresh and big swa lors like these, it really reminds me of the gigantic swa lor and maybe ang kar as well which chuan provided back in their days at bedok reservoir. Prawns were deshelled till the last prawn tip without needing to crack the last bit of shell. This is really for the prawn enjoyers so that they can savour the entire prawn without any effort needed, really appreciate the attention to details here.
Very fresh ingredients and even the pork lard were crispy and don't have the old oil taste. Their chilli are just nice and not spicy at all, everyone can get to try it. The prawn stock used to fry the hkm also is filled with Umami goodness. Umami just keeps getting better and better! Easily top 5 in my favorite hkm to return to list.

posts.author: Teochew Alex
posts.text:
This is a story of a old school style hokkien mee
https://www.facebook.com/share/p/14hyxvpAiYx/?mibextid=wwXIfr
Hokkien Mee Showdown: The Old-School Eggy Revival
To me, Hokkien Mee comes in 4 distinct styles:
the wok hei infused dry version, the wet and prawny type, and the old-school wet eggy sauce version and th now rarely seen pure sotong and or lala style.
Today’s spotlight is on the third: the old-school wet eggy style.
What sets this version apart is its unmistakable fried egg intensity. From the very first bite, you get a bold, full-bodied flavour of egg infused deeply with rich prawn broth. In a well-executed plate, the noodles release their starch during cooking, creating that signature silky, cohesive stickiness. It’s not the cloying kind, rather, a smooth, almost velvety consistency that slides down effortlessly.
There used to be a legendary stall, 金海 at Circuit Road, that served one of the best renditions of this eggy style. Sadly, it closed before COVID, another classic lost to time.
Today, I turn to a humble stall,Hoe 和
What keeps me coming back isn’t just the portion size (though many swear by it), but something more meaningful: progress. I’ve tasted their Hokkien Mee from pre-COVID days till now, and the improvement in skill and consistency is undeniable. Their current eggy version is arguably their best yet, more refined, more balanced, and more confident.
For this style of Hokkien Mee, I strongly recommend eating it on the spot. The eggy gravy, while luscious when fresh, tends to turn overly “niam” (sticky and dense) when dabaoed and left sitting too long.
This is a plate best enjoyed fresh off the wok, when the egg aroma is at its peak, and the texture is just right.
Hoe Hokkien Mee 和Hoe
North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre. 
861 North Bridge Rd, Singapore 198783
Rating: can eat on spot 
#HokkienMee #hawkersg #美食耳朵  #foodeats #teochewalex

$8 + $2 prawns and $2 sotong. Wet style, good woh hei and a savory broth with a tinge of sweetness. Although I added $2 worth of sotong, there were just tiny scraps of sotong and mostly heads and tail. Just note that the pork and sotong are sliced into very tiny bits so it is hardly noticeable that they actually added more. Other than that, it’s still enjoyable and every now and then I come back for this wet and medium sized bee hoon version of HKM. There is also more bee hoon than other stalls, which makes it less hard to digest.

Much has been posted and much has been said about this HKM located in a relatively quiet hawker centre which is itself located in the MacPherson HDB housing estate. … See more
Jeremy
Much has been posted and much has been said about this HKM located in a relatively quiet hawker centre which is itself located in the MacPherson HDB housing estate. 

I happened to be in MacPherson yesterday at about 7:00 pm and hungry and decided to make at pit stop at 80 Circuit Rd where this hawker centre is located.

I wasn’t aware that their closing time was 7:00 pm and the staff there, 2 men and a woman, were busy cleaning up! The woman saw me and said that there are some freshly fried HKM that were already pre-packed and placed in a cooler box and asked me if I wanted it! I said OK and paid $6 and was given a complimentary small bottle of water too.

I opened the double layer brown paper packaging and there was a strong whiff of HKM emerging and a pool of chilli on one side.

I decided not to have too much chilli and pushed most of it to one side as I do not want the the chilli sauce to overpower the taste of the HKM. Fortunately it was good decision as the remaining chilli sauce that was already embedded in the HKM had a strong spicy overtone that had me perspiring!

Standard HKM ingredients were present including prawns, sotong, belly pork and pork lard too however the three mid-sized prawns were not succulently fresh! 

A faint HKM umami was present and taste was acceptable, however I prefer a fresh fried plate of HKM rather than one that had already been pre-packaged! 

I will endeavour to make another trip here to eat it freshly fried before I made a judgement of whether it will make it to my personal list of best HKM but I guessed I will have to come before 7 pm!

posts.author: HandsomeBison2617
posts.text:
Fatty Cat Hokkien Mee
Saw that there isn't many review so here's my personal verdict: 4/10
- Thick yellow mee and bee hoon used, giving a chewy texture almost like laksa noodle. Personal preference is thin bee hoon because it works better on holding onto the thick zhup
- The zhup is very thick, but not flavourful. When eaten hot, there is no seafood taste and no wok hei at all. But once it cooled down, you can taste a slight sweetness in the broth.
- The lack of smokiness is very obvious when you visit the stall, majority of the cooking is steaming the noodle and the wok has almost no smoke coming out of it
- Pork lard is slightly crispy, but oily when you bite into it. Those who like fung yi's super crispy and not jelat pork lard will not be a fan of this
- Prawn was fresh, chewy and bouncy with slight sweetness. Good quality, but 2 pieces for $6 portion
- Chilli was belacan type, but more towards sweet and sour combination. Was honestly quite good and helped made the HKM much more nicer
Ok if you're around the area and want to satisfy craving, but the hawker definitely has a lot of other better options if you're there. For a normal person who isn't very critical about HKM, maybe rating about 6/10. Can eat, but not mind-blowing or memorable.
Location: Holland drive market & food centre

posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
Neighbourwok @ Bukit Batok
My second time trying and that’s because I happen to be catching up with someone around that area.
$10 for the “big prawn” (3 pieces) version. Probably equivalent to most $8 versions and the prawns are indeed slightly larger than the above average sizes.
I describe Neighbourwok as Ah Jie with slightly less wok hei and umami. Very similar in style. Even the pork lard is very similar (oil type and very crunchy) with same plate and similar chilli. What you see in the picture was already added with “extra pork lard”. Vietnamese lady taking orders said “only 2-3 pieces more for free but If you want anymore you need to pay 50 cents.”. Not complaining, just to manage your expectations. One thing I find very disconnected is that whether you order $5/ $6 or $10, the amount of pork lard given to you is seldom about the portion or amount of money you pay. It’s just always that “one tablespoon” or their own yardstick used to measure a single standard portion. Anyway, just an observation but it shouldn’t be rocket science. I believe if you order a bigger plate or when you add ingredients till it’s almost double the price of a standard small plate, you should get a proportionate amount of pork lard.
Anyway, it’s decent but I won’t travel there when I have Ah jie just around the corner and better still another one of my recent favourite nearby me is Jackson HKM which is also the similar style (wet with medium bee hoon). The slurpy-licious version.
177 Bukit Batok West Ave. 8, Get Together Coffeeshop, Singapore 650177

posts.author: Alvin Pancakie
posts.text:
Had a chance to try 3 hkm again back to back
1. Fung Yi Delights Hokkien Mee Orh Luak
844 Tampines St 82, Singapore 520844
Most probably the best out of the three hkm tried today .
Flavorful, Umami , and the most heavily seasoned out of the three . For people who are more 重口味, this is most probably one of the best but for people looking for more depth and less seasoned and more well balanced prawn noodles then maybe not
No wok hei present , only thing that was fried was the egg and simmered in stock with noodles . Recorded the time to be 6-7 mins per wok which is insanely fast . The hkm is basically carried by the prawn stock and lots of fish sauce and seasoning . For Chuan I believe the time to be around 10-12 mins . Maybe that’s why it tasted more like simmered braised noodles that are barely fried . But that is most probably one of the best for these style of wet simmered hkm
As there are barely any maillard reaction happening between the eggs , noodles and lard , i get the heavily seasoned stock as it will be the only way to provide depth the the dish
Other than that LARD probably best , its a part of the pork fat that connect with the skin , which provides two different kind of texture and crunch .
Chili have a nice heat to it and noodle texture is good
I get why it is the best for some people and maybe gelat for some and bad for some .
I do appreciate the swa lor served , Sotong feels abit tough and chewy and abit on the tasteless side
2. Jackson Fried Hokkien Mee
152 Serangoon North Ave. 2, #01-354 The Nook, Singapore 550152
Newly reopened and 1 min walk from Xiao di
Waited close to 10 mins to get my plate .
It’s very different style than Xiao di , it’s not flooded with stock and have a dry creamy consistency . Texture is superb .
Nothing to complain abt the lard . But the sambal feels abit less 香. Like it is less seasoned and belecan taste feel like can have more of it .
The hkm is very prawn forward , savoury and umami in its own right . But I feel like it lacks depth , the flavour lingers but feels stuck and umami and savoury and prawny and nothing more .
Also no wok hei present . Like none for all 3 hkm tried .
Again some people will hate it some people will love it and defend it but I think there are rooms for improvement for the overall taste of the hkm
Swa Lor is either served or the small Angkar , note that there aren’t any Sotong
3. Xiao Di Fried Prawn Noodle
153 Serangoon North Ave 1, #01-512, Singapore 550153
Most probably the most balanced tasting out of the three . But like the other 2 it’s a simmered noodles and again some people absolutely love this style
Lard is good , sambal feels to watery but I guess it’s more for mixing than adding it bit by bit . Lard is crispy even when soaked so that’s good
Texture of the noodles is apt .
Stock is more towards sweet , savoury kind with the sweetness hitting at the back of the tongue .
No wok hei just barely fried and simmered in flooded
Normal vanamei prawns

posts.author: Jane Ng
posts.text:
OLD HUP: Surprised to find a Food Court HKM whose boss actually cares to do this 
Honestly, i wouldnt say its the best i have had, but i believe those who can taste layers & the raw ingredients used in dishes would be able to tell how much effort this boss made. From broth to chilli.
Ah, ignore the missing pork lard, i didnt ask for it.
[ OLD HUP KEE @ Waterway Point (Koufu) ]
They have 3 outlets in sg i heard.
Small plate
Its a mixed between zhi char HKM & Wok Hey heavy ones.
*(just note, dont expect crazy wok hey taste)
Noodles - ZERO Alkaline taste, took in all the broth well
Broth - Umami, balanced, ending collagen smooth. Not drama diabetic & Kidney failure kind.
Chilli - Crazy Chilli lovers can attempt it proper, this cuts through the noodles spice forward.
For wholesome taste, dab the sauce into every mouth if need be, Else, dont need to. Noodles can standalone itself. (Oh, you can ask for their signature Sambal Chilli too, it's good!)
It took me about 8mins to clear this, the aftermath - i just felt like eating another 3 mouths before i would want to end the experience. No thirst after eating yet satisfying broth aftertaste lingering in mouth.
Disclaimer: I wasnt hungry, so mind and tummy were conscious, judgement not clouded 
Of course, F&B, expect varied experiences la, my personal 2 cents.
If Anything, i think the boss's hotline is available.. (i did text him saying his HKM is edible and thanked him for a balanced, no diabetic HBP experience)..
Next stop, First Street!

posts.text:
Finally got a chance to try Yi Ji from Old Airport Road hawker centre. Come weekday lunchtime, no queue.
My review is based on "tapao" version. After ordering I saw Aunty fry it very wet and I also noticed it was ladled from a pre-fried batch. 
I'm in the dry HKM camp but if tapao I find a bit more gravy keeps the noodles moist when you reach home and the noodles are more flavourful after it absorbs the gravy.
3 prawns, a bit of belly pork and no sotong but 2 slivers of mock abalone? 
Noodles portion was generous and thats about the only positive. Despite the extra gravy the noodles were almost bland with zero wok hei. The accompanying belacan was more on the sour side which did little to elevate the dish.
Overall I found it slightly better than its neighbour 2 stalls down and much nicer than that over rated Nam Sing. If I'm at Old Airport this is the stall I will order from but not make a HKM pilgrimage from afar.

posts.author: Alvin Pancakie
posts.text:
There have been a post on this group lately that highlight on black bits
Most of the time there will be black bits in the hkm . I also realise it and usually it comes more from fried egg and garlic.
Sadly to say it is there present in cast iron wok at least . People who say eh never clean properly have never clean their wok before or their mouth . You say eh I clean so clean no black bits at home why your one have . Obviously you only use your wok like how much you use your brain , to throughly wash ur wok , without the black bits there , the only way is to use the steel wool . And it takes ages . So if you expect your brain to not be frustrated at how slow it is , it is almost impossible to clean it to no black bits .
Then after cleaning it so clean , you think cast iron don’t rust ? You need to season it . Just to let you know the whole process takes like 15 mins plus . To layer the oil one after the other . Ever season wok will at least have black bits one way or the other , also dependent on how much it’s fried on . Sometimes it is unavoidable
I recently been to fungyi and that is the cleanest I have seen . Boss took a bloody paint scrapper to scrap the wok . That’s most probably the best way to get rid of the black bits . But guess what , photos that I scan through on google review and also on this group , it is still there , but it’s the best I have seen . But if you think everyone have the same time and effort just eat pasta from sauce pan or Maggie mee and I believe if you are so concern about black bits just don’t eat hkm at all , go with salad or healthy vegan food

posts.author: Gopalsamy Rajkumar
posts.text:
https://maps.app.goo.gl/kVZRBWB1pWHUagGi9?g_st=ac
Recently, I saw a post about disgusting burnt bits in FHM. Some people think it’s wok-hey, but I feel it’s just result from a dirty wok. If the wok isn’t cleaned properly, leftover noodles stick, burn and break off into the dish. Over time, every stir‑fry scrapes more burnt scraps into the food. That’s bitterness, not wok-hey.
Foodies who love wok-hey defend it, but I think too many burnt bits show poor wok hygiene. I had bad experiences at Uncle Peter and Bao Er for all my visits, every plate came with those charred bits, which really turned me off. Burnt food isn’t healthy either, once in a while is fine, but eating it often isn’t good.
That’s why I enjoy 618 Hokkien Mee. Never once did I get burnt bits there. Maybe I’m lucky or maybe boss really cleans her wok between batches. The taste is decent, the prawns are sweet, pork lards are good and the portion is generous. For me, that’s value for money, I don’t need wok-hey for my FHM, just clean, tasty noodles will brighten up my day.
Address: Block 618, Yishun Ring Road, Singapore 760618

posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
Umami
$6+$4 ingredients + $1 egg.
There is not only pork lard but pork skin. Airy and crispy but on the harder side. Pork lard was also good as it didn’t have the stale after taste. Today’s plate had a very sticky, chewy, and noodle goodness with a balanced broth. Prawns were one of the best tasting, tender and sweet with shells peeled all the way and leaving only the tail end so that you won’t need to bite carefully to expel that 1 cm of prawn meat. A very first in the industry but something I find very ingenious. I will also do that for my home cooked HKM going forward. Eggs were really nicely charred. Overall a very pleasant dish to have.
Do visit or revisit. Remember to take the chilli from the bottle instead of the box, which I agree is that darker and not so impressive chilli. Better off just saving your time to prepare two types of chilli and only provide the bottled one which was much better. Those are who can’t handle too much spice just use less of the bottled one. Win-win situation there so just for consideration to save your time. Great effort on the improvements along the way.
709 Geylang Rd, Singapore 389624

comments.author: Edwin Ng
comments.text:
One thing I can’t stand is when people say the KL Hokkien Mee is the best and original. Mostly they are Malaysians who have just tried our HKM and judged it from that one mediocre experience. If they like dark soy sauce so much just buy a bottle and drink it. As we all know, there is so much depth to the dish (Singapore HKm).
The broth itself, preparing it, is more complex than any other hawker dish based on time taken and complexity and number of ingredients. When you include the frying and the chilli sauce, there is just nothing to be compared to in the Singapore and KL hawker fares. Nothing I can think of.
In case you don’t know…what goes into our Singapore HKM broth:- Prawn shells, dried hae bee, clams, pork skin, chicken feet, chicken bones, pork bones with the pork, squid, and prawns all cooked into the broth. Some can even use ikan bilis, flower crab, etc. all just to make the broth. One thing I can’t stand is when people say the KL Hokkien Mee is the best and original. https://maps.app.goo.gl/EwHJSaZ64m1dxasx8
Everytime when I visit Seah Im Food Centre, I will definitely support Cheng Ji and order extra. This might just be an average plate of FHM and some people may even say it doesn’t taste great. But every time i visit here, i come with a different mindset. I’m not here chasing the “BEST” meal, I’m here to appreciate the kindness this elderly couple has shown their regulars over the years.  
Those who know them understand their generosity. They keep prices low so workers in the area can still enjoy a decent meal with big prawns. Out of consideration, they even avoid pork and lard so Malay boatmen and ship crew can eat there too.  
Some people may think they are rude, but many don’t know what they’ve experienced. In the past, people would take chopsticks, spoons or even chilli without buying anything from them. If you actually order, they always give extra chilli willingly. It’s also hard to understand when some customers say their food is expensive and try to share a $4 plate, yet have no issue spending much more on drinks from places like starbucks or chagee.
Uncle looks very weak now and I’m not sure how much longer Cheng Ji will continue at Seah Im Food Centre. Hope they can continue as long as they can and wish Uncle and Aunty 身体健康.  
Address: 2 Seah Im Road, #01-59 Seah Im Food Centre, Singapore 099114 See less

posts.author: Kitty Ong
posts.text:
SG Umami - 709 Geylang Road
Chef Alvin is definitely a fan of HKM because his plate of HKM brings glimpses of tribute to the good things from other names in the HKM scene.
A good proportion of noodles vs beehoon is fried in high heat to lock in the flavours of the rich unami savoury stock for a semi dry finish.
There are hints of You Fu, Chuan and Rainbow Rice House in the taste and its the kind of savouriness (even with a slight bitter from the prawn head butter) that I personally like.
I had the $8 plate.
Alvin also has 2 kinds of lard on offer .. the usual smaller pieces lard is not overly crispy but had the fragrance of fresh lard melts in with the heat from the HKM to be released into a good burst of flavour.
the bigger crispy ones reminds me of Fung Yi's ultra crispy pork rinds and will satisfy many who like their lard to have the keropok texture.
There are even 2 types of chilli on offer ! the less spicy one has sweet afternotes like a good nasi lemak sambal that adds a welcomed sweetness when mixed with the unami bombed HKM.
the spicy chilli offers good enough heat but not overpower the good taste of the HKM and yet elevate the flavour of the seafood.
Special mention that there is NO surcharge to dapao -
Umami uses the good old brown dapao paper to lock in the flavours instead of charging us 30cents for plastic containers.
But having said that, full marks to Umami for having a special container for lard, chilli and lime without charge that helps to make sure the condiments do not get soggy by the time you reach home with your dapao.
I think the little things matter and I believe Alvin is someone who takes the customer experience very seriously and I wish many more will come and support Umami.

明知山有虎，偏向虎山行。
First of all, congratulations on Fung Yi Delights’ second outlet opening. With another very popular FHM stall in the same block, most hawkers cooking the same dish would probably try to avoid such direct competition.
But Boss Kenny 也不是省油的灯, his cooking has improved tremendously over the past two years since I first tried it back in July 2024. He definitely has his own fans and supporters, and has proven that 酒香不怕巷子深. Even opening at a less convenient location won’t be an issue for foodies, who will always find their way there.
Beyond taste, one of the reasons I like Fung Yi is the quality of his ingredients. The freshness, the change in the type of sotong used compared to the earlier days and his choice of swa lor for FHM all elevate the overall experience to the next level.
Besides FHM, this second outlet doesn’t have fried oyster, but they do serve carrot cake. I tried their prawn carrot cake and it was very delicious too.
Address: Block 69 Bedok South Avenue 3, #01-468, Singapore 460069

posts.author: Samuel Lim
posts.text:
This is not meant to be a post to rank the top HKM, just a post comparing 3 HKM stalls in the east. 
Comparing three Hokkien mee stalls in the East: Funyi (red plate), Bedok 69 (white plate), and Shiok Bedok (black plate).
Funyi’s broth leans sweet and suits those who prefer a milder profile without wok hei, and who don’t enjoy noodles to be well fried. There’s no option to remove bean sprouts. The lard is semi crunchy, and the waiting time can be quite long. The chilli, however, delivers a good kick.
Shiok Bedok stands out for intensity. It has the strongest wok hei of the three, leaning towards a charred, almost burnt profile. The noodles are extremely well fried with a pronounced char. The stock is also on the sweeter side, and there’s no option to remove bean sprouts. Waiting time is long, but manageable with a buzzer system. The chilli is the best of the three which is spicy, tangy, and very addictive.
In my opinion, Bedok 69 offers the best overall balance. There’s a mild wok hei, and the broth is savoury with more depth. The noodles are well fried, and you can request no bean sprouts. The lard is very crispy and is one of the best I’ve had and not overly greasy. The chilli is nicely balanced, with spice and a slight tang, though it does come with quite a bit of seeds.
Which Hokkien mee would you choose? See less

Some of the things I tried these two weeks
1.Steven Fried Rice
Main items seems to be focus on fried rice , why they included hkm , maybe because they do Penang prawn noodles . But I always believe , good prawn stock does not translate to a good fried hkm . The state it is at feels like any other food republic hkm or any tzi char stall hkm , besides rainbow house , kind of hkm , bland , unprocessed and totally feels more like Lor mee than an actually fried prawn noodles , it’s 6.50 and comes with the 2 tiniest prawn I have ever seen
Address : 5 Upper Boon Keng Rd
2. Neighbourwok @ Clementi Mall
Decent , but nothing wow compared to their stall at Bukit Batok .
Have always believed that it takes more than a few years time to actually teach someone the trade of frying the noodles and the basic of the dish heck even I am learning something from it everyday but just without a mentor .
Pork lard is good , chili on point , stock feels very mild and so does that neighbourwok that is signature to the dish . $6.90 for the smallest but aircon environment so can’t really complain much . Portion is smaller than usual small . Overall decent plate but would consider visiting original outlet at bb to get the original profile of the dish

posts.author: Eric Widjaja
posts.text:
Disappointing Hokkien Mee Experience at My Favourite Spot
Brought someone new to try one of my favourite but sad to say, today's plate was way below expectations. The moment the plate came out I know it was going to be below the usual standards. The mushy outlook, the slightly expanded yellow noodles, and the size of the prawns, and right off the bat, eating the first mouth , disappointment was all I felt. Only your chilli is still maintaining the usual kick and that helps me to TRY and finish my plate.
Shiok Hokkien Mee I am still one of your biggest fan, so I hope that you realize that consistency is the hardest factor to maintain in fnb. I understand that you open more and more outlets because you were doing well, but however you do well because the chefs were good, they maintained the standard and they kept it there. I can say out of 20 times I eat at your stalls, 19 of them were positive and I left the place smiling. Prawns were mostly fresh and big, noodles were perfectly cooked with no alkaline taste, and the mashed up thin beehoon and yellow noodles were so good that I just can't get enough of it, wanting more every single bite.
Today, your sk outlet came out a female chef, my guess is it's a new chef, nothing against her , but I can say that the standard of the HKM has dropped way below, until my wife and I can't finish 2 normal plates, jelat came into picture. Then my wife asked me " why the HKM so different nowadays ? " I shrugged, and replied, new chef lor.
Consider this a feedback, maybe this is the direction Shiok wants to go, open more outlets but standards drop, maybe you can gain more popularity by opening new outlets in new area, but you will definitely lose your loyal fans if you continue to drop the standards offered in your various outlets.

Sing Hi Fry
Ordered $5 with additional ingredients (think was $3.80) + 80 cents egg. Portion was quite big and taste reminded me of the typical Tze char ones like Bugis and Rainbow rice house, although probably not as good as them. Broth was mild, but texture of noodles and egg were more like Tze char wet style. The chilli was good.
Overall, above average but not great. I would try only if you’re in the area (now crowded, not hot, easy to park, cheap for the portion). I think 309 is still a bit better and around the corner so If you have not tried, I’d go with Blk 309’s hokkien mee first.
Blk 322 Hougang Ave 5, Yen Fei Lai eating house, Singapore 530322

posts.text:
https://maps.app.goo.gl/1SEpp6xfmd7WZ8Xk6
Like many others, I also joined the $2 promo at Boss Daniel’s 777 coffeeshop since it’s just 5 minutes from my place. The crowd was insane, the whole coffeeshop was packed even at around 2am. I ordered hokkien mee, fried oyster, carrot cake, mee pok and mee kia. I wanted to try the western food and chicken rice too, but the waiting time was easily over an hour. Honestly, I came with zero expectations because it’s tough to keep quality when they’re rushing so many orders. The FHM and carrot cake both had a burnt taste. The carrot cake taste was still okay since I ordered the black version, but the FHM was overcooked, soggy and bland. Luckily, their sambal belacan which reminds me of Uncle Peter saved it. Their fried oyster was crispy but totally tasteless. Surprisingly, the Mee pok and Mee kia were the best among all my orders. The cook didn’t bother with the crazy crowd and just did his thing, so the taste was pretty good. Overall, it was a fun Labour Day promo and I salute all the staffs for working extra hard. Even though I saw some cooks frustrated in the kitchen, throwing plates and containers, they still kept things going.
Address: Block 51 Lor 6 Toa Payoh, #01-60/62, Singapore 310051

posts.author: Gopalsamy Rajkumar
posts.text:
https://maps.app.goo.gl/YJjYa9CX8HX54fyK8?g_st=ac
First time trying this stall after missing them twice when they were closed. Tastewise, it wasn’t bad, though the prawn stock could have been more robust. No wok-hey but their ingredients were excellent. Succulent prawns, tender sotong and juicy pork belly. The pork lard was average, while the sambal belacan leaned more towards sour than spicy. The main downside was the noodles, they turned out too soggy. Despite using thick bee hoon, which usually holds up better in the wok compared to thin bee hoon, the yellow noodles ended up overly soft with no texture. I sat there for more than half an hour and saw many people ordering FHM. The boss scooped all the noodles and bee hoon from the same batch that had been sitting in the wok for some time, so it wasn’t surprising that my order came within a minute. Overall, this plate had many good points, but the noodles were really a letdown.
Address: Block 226H, Ang Mo Kio Street 22, #01-22, Singapore 568226

posts.author: Albert Wilson
posts.text:
I arrived at 12:30 pm. First, I must say the chefs are very friendly and always smiling. They informed me that the wait would be about 40 minutes, which was fine for me as it was peak hour.
I ordered the $8 version with three big white prawns. The prawns were very, very fresh. The sotong was also very fresh and succulent. The FHKM was creamy, with just the right level of wetness. It had a sticky texture — ahem — just nice. The umami was just right, and the wok hei was also just right. Even from where I was sitting, about 5m away, I could smell it.
The lard was fresh and crispy, adding that extra oomph to an already good plate of FHKM. There are two types of chilli. I think a 1:2 ratio, with more of the lighter one, works best. Don’t ignore the nasi lemak chilli too, as it is good.
Although this stall is still pretty new, it whips up a high-standard FHKM that suits my taste. I will definitely come again. Highly recommended.
Umami
709 Geylang Rd, Singapore 389624 See less

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
Didn’t know this stall was near me. 
Went there with the intend to try the famous Hougang orh jian. However this HKM stall hidden and tucked into a corner of the coffeeshop caught my eye. Heard of the name before but I vaguely remember it was in the west side? So mai tu liao, die die must try!
Was there about 1.45pm. Not much queue and they just finished a batch, so needed to wait about 10 mins for a new batch. Ordered the $8 plate and it was quite a huge serving. Lime and chilli was self service. Pork lard was giving without asking. The chilli is the bright red belachan type, not my fav type of chilli but it’s ok.
Looks wise it’s an extremely gooey plate. I can see loads of chunky pork belly, extremely generous with the pork belly. There was sotong as well, but chopped into quite small pieces. 3 small size prawns. First taste, some wok hei and very umami taste of the prawn stock. Love the tasty gooey sauce and the noodles still has some bite to it which I really like. It’s not mushy noodles. There was seriously alot of pork belly chunks, the meatiest HKM I’ve eaten. Almost every spoonful has pork belly. Prawns were fresh, but sotong I feel it’s chopped too small and become slightly overcooked. Pork lard was fresh and crispy! Chilli wise, not my type of chilli but it’s decent, and elevates the dish with a slight kick. 
Overall it is a good plate for me. If you like gooey HKM and al Dante noodles, this is for you! For $8, it was super filling for a big sized guy like me. 
They do take cashless payments using SGQR. Paid with Diner’s UnionPay card via SGQR gives me a decent 2% rebate! No minimum monthly spend.  
P.S. I also ordered the famous Hougang fried oyster FYI if you’re wondering.

Craving Hokkien mee today. Wanted to tahan one more day, but Umami Geylang isn’t open tomorrow and my favourite Bedok 69 Hokkien Mee (not Fungyi) wasn’t open today, so I decided to head over to Tampines 1 to try Hokkien Man Hokkien mee.

Ordered the large plate for $9.90. No beansprouts by default, which is a plus for me. The noodles tasted sweet overall, and even the chilli was sweet rather than spicy. I prefer savoury over sweet. The lard semi crispy on the outside, soft and airy on the inside. 

What I couldn’t stand, though, was the amount of burnt bits in the noodles. I know it’s hard to avoid completely, but this one really had a lot.

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
You know what they say, never trust a hawker which advertises with things like “Best”, “No.1 in SG” etc, or those who put their faces on their sign board. 
Heard about this stall a while ago and finally had the chance to try it. 
The pricing structure was also not the usual, $7 small, $13.50 medium and $20 large. A hungry single diner (like me) probably won’t order the $13.50 one. So I just ordered the $7 one. First glance, honestly was kinda disappointed and my first thought was “siao liao, sure jiak buay pah”. Hope the taste makes up for it. 
So for $7, we get 2 small/medium prawns, a few slices of pork belly, no sotong but replaced with 2 slices of fake abalone which is also made of squid anyway. Chilli wise is the type I like, sambal. There seems to be more thin bee hoon than yellow mee, so good for bee hoon lovers. Stock is quite gooey too. No pork lard given too (not sure if they serve it as I didn’t ask). 
First taste, not much of wok hei, great umami taste from the stock. I can’t really tell what’s in the stock, but it’s not just prawns. It’s more like a seafood stock rather than a prawn stock. It reminds me of those zi char seafood noodles instead of Hokkien Mee. For me, the noodles felt abit under cooked as both the bee hoon and yellow mee still had quite a bit of bite. Prawns were fresh, and the pork belly and fake abalone were just normal. Chilli was the usual factory sambal, nice and salty with a slight spicy kick. 
Overall it’s an ok plate for me. Would not travel purposely to eat this, and to be honest, $7 is a bit on the pricy side. My guess is probably from the “ho liao” that goes into the stock. They accept cashless payments. 
P.S. end of the meal, really jiak buay pah 
 walked to the hawker centre beside and chanced upon this Yang’s epok epok which was pretty good. $1.20 an epok was pricey but the filling was Gao Gao.. See less

Finally unboxing my maiden take of Ah Jie after much positive reviews by bros & sis..
Ordered at 12.20pm & got it in abt 15mins (as pre-empted by the stall attendant) - shorter than I expected bcos spotted a few dine-ins also waiting..
$8 got me this full box of flavouful, well-balanced wet mix of yellow noodles:thick bh (50:50), 4 small-medium prawns, 3 really tiny sotong rings (qualm #1), thin pork belly strips (qualm #2), egg, fragrant pork lard bits (which I prefer to chunkier ones), topped with refreshing tangy chilli & lime. No chives though. Although FHM is suitable for tabao, not many stalls do it well. This is one that does. Will return for dine-in when there is chance in future.
Thanks for the recommendation!

posts.author: Takeda Bushido
posts.text:
This is it. One of the ultimate traditional style hkm done right. Been a while since I came here as the previous 2 times the hkm cooked by the vietnam guy chef was unpalatable. Been seeing posts of yang zhou hkm at 40 beo crescent #01-16 popped up every now and then so decided to patronize it again. 
Upon reaching, I realized it was the familiar vietnamese lady who fried one of the best and nostalgic plate of hkm I've ever tasted in SG. I ordered the $6 plate and it came with so many fresh pieces of sotong, prawns and even fresh pork lard. The style of this hkm really reminds me of the old school gim chew hkm at bedok hawker when the grandfather/grandmother were still around manning the wok. It also kind of resembles a bit of tian tian lai hkm at tpy which is the 'Chinese carbonara' style hkm with hints of garlicky taste. U can call this hkm a collab between gim chew (old school) x tian tian lai with more umami.
Do not expect wok hei or whatsoever as the main highlight of this dish is not about wok hei, it is about reliving the traditional old school taste of hkm and those who ate the old school type of hkm will concur with me. See less

Do not expect wok hei or whatsoever as the main highlight of this dish is not about wok hei, it is about reliving the traditional old school taste of hkm and those who ate the old school type of hkm will concur with me.

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
So I had to give 309 a try again after recently trying the 322 HKM. Been awhile since I been to 309 and boy there were some changes. 
First of all, prices increased from $5 to $5.50 since 15 May 2026. Secondly, they now only have a Paynow QR code instead of the SGQR, which means that I can’t use my Diner’s app to pay which gives me 2% rebate with no min spend on their UnionPay card. Lastly, maybe I came late, around 2.30pm, but it’s the lady who’s frying. She tried to sell me one of those pre-packed HKM which I have no idea how long it has been sitting on the counter. Luckily she was ok to fry a new plate for me to dine in. 
Received my plate in about 10 mins, fresh and piping hot. 2 limes were given but the chilli at first was like half a teaspoon amount, had to self service take another big scoop. Well, I love and prefer sambal after all. 
First look, portion seems a bit smaller than usual. First bite, wok hei was there but slightly lacking compared to 322. Umami and prawny stock taste was good. Sotong was fresh and pork belly was nice and tender. Only complain were the prawns. Kinda small.. tiny… I was expecting more for $5.50 esp. with the increased price of $0.50. The best was the lard. Nice and crispy! 
Anyway, my final thought is that this 309 HKM is still good. I love their sambal and the lard, though the wok hei is not as strong as 322. Oh and I heard 309 they are changing owner soon, so I’ll be back again to test water again. See less

posts.author: Dick Long
posts.text:
Beo Crescent Yangzhou Hokkien Mee
Came by to try after seeing good review by Tony Chia.
I must say I am impressed, this Hokkien Mee has improved leaps and bounds and I feel it’s almost 618’s standard.
My portion is $5 and it has 2 prawns which is fresh and crunchy, about 6 sotong rings, some were cooked nicely but about a couple is hard.
The lady chef is cooking a fresh wok for about 3 orders including mine, look at the smoke from her wok. And she is serious with her cooking I must say.
The noodles were soaked in the broth which was gooey and taste nice, no wok hei here but the umami is power. I don’t take chili with hokkien mee so no comments but the pork lard is fresh and crispy and kept in another air tight container, you have to request for it but they are generous with it once you ask.
Had a chat with the chef Ah Zhen and she shared that recently they have this $5 portion because there are many seniors in this area who are quite price sensitive, so she brought back the $5 portion which is actually sufficient and just nice.
Then I was telling her about our Hokkien Mee Hunting group and showed her Tony’s post and I saw her eyes lit up and she was so excited to know that Tony posted about her.
Address in the last picture of their Google business profile. Give them a chance again and I believe you will be just as impressed as me.

Adjust Your Expectations.
Mr Uncle
Block 226A Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1
#01-629
SG 561226
It was in late March this year. I had placed the order via FoodPanda. I was amused by the menu on the app as the photo and description did not match. And I was guessing that the actual dish would probably resemble the photo. 
Okay, came the version of yellow noodles and thin rice noodles mixed together. Still, it is not the HKM that most of us would expect as there were leafy greens and other veggies like carrot and cauliflower in it too. Prawns had their shells on. Sotong was not the fully white, ring kind. Had the very homemade vibe with parts of purplish tint. Lime and sambal chilli were provided.
Overall, taste is okay. But objectively, this is a fried noodles dish rather than the type of HKM featured in this group. I supposed it is a cultural difference issue. I ordered hor fun as well, but kueh teow was used.
Mr Uncle also has an outlet at Sembawang, based on what I saw from their carrier bags. See less

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
For those who feel my post is too long, just read this tl;dr (Too Lazy; Didn’t Read) summary - Hokkien Mee fans, this stall is worth a try at least once. Really surprised with the wok hei, but I am concerned about the consistency. Everything is nicely cooked except for the overcooked prawns and Lao Hong lard.
So anyway, back to the review. Most people I know will probably never like to eat at their “house downstairs” for all sorts of reasons. “Nice meh?”, “Eat until sian liao..”, “I rather go where and where, much better”. 
So I might be a little late, but I recently found out about this stall at my “house downstairs”. Well not exactly downstairs, but just 2 blocks away.
I arrived for a late lunch, around 1.45pm. No queue at all. They have $5 and $7. Ordered the $5 plate and saw the guy taking some pre-fried noodles and re-frying it in a smaller wok. Noticed that the fire was super strong, and I know that the wok hei going to be power. There was another guy, frying another big batch of hokkien mee in the bigger wok. 
First looks, the color looks kinda off. Smell is heavenly, and some lard bits were given. There was also 2 medium sized prawns which looked kinda overcooked, and some sotong rings and pork belly chunks. Chilli wise is the belachan kinda and was self service with small dishes to scoop the chili which I like, so my noodles won’t be affected if I don’t like the chili.
After the mandatory “lime in”, my first bite and oh boy, just as I guessed correctly, the wok hei is SUPER STRONG. Flavors were all there and I just can’t stop eating it, noodles were cooked nicely, soft but not mushy. Sotong was fresh and cooked nicely, pork belly was meaty and tender. Only gripe are the prawns, they were such a good size but sadly they were overcooked. Still edible though, but the mouthfeel was just funny. Pork lard was just a few pieces and sadly, it was already soft and Lao Hong. As for the chilli, it was kinda spicy for me and honestly, the noodles are so tasty that no chili is required. What I noticed was that if you put too little chill, you can’t taste any chilli. But if you add too much chili, it covers the wok hei and umami flavors. End up I ditched the chili and ate it as it was.
All in all, this was a really good plate. Super value for money for $5 and I was really surprised to find such a stall just so near to me. Hokkien mee lovers, this stall is worth at least a try once. I have also tasted the nearby Blk 309 one, and in my honest opinion, this one has stronger wok hei and bolder flavors. 
After my meal, as I was sipping my Kopi O Kosong Peng, I was thinking the wok hei could be so strong maybe because my plate was fried separately in a smaller wok with a powerful burner which I think is used to fry their fried rice. I am not sure if the same wok hei can be achieved if it was during crowded lunch time where plates are most likely scooped from the big wok batch of noodles. For this, I think I will return to try again to confirm.
P.S. My Kopi O Kosong Peng cost $1.90 from the coffee shop drinks stall. Is this the norm? Personally I feel it’s on the steep side. Opinions? See less

posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee @ Whampoa Food Center
Normally don’t get to eat HKM on weekends but today was an exception as we are all going to be away from any hawker fare for some time. Decided on Whampoa food center and noticed that the famous HKM is already open.
Ordered a $5+$2 ingredients. Not noticeable wokhei, very mild umami prawn forward broth, and semi wet and slurpy minus the -licious. When I was waiting (15 mins wait at 445pm!), the broth smelled really awesome but somehow that didn’t translate to a flavorful dish. Prawns were tiny and nothing spectacular. No pork and sotong went unnoticed and didn’t leave much of an impression. Overall, just above average 6.5/10 range. I will not try again - life is short. For me, I will only revisit >=8 point stalls.
I don’t know why their business is so good but I personally feel that stalls that hype themselves up by making people wait at their stalls tend to be able to generate hype. By giving out buzzers, it makes the wait feel much less and gathering people at the stall creates that impression of supply < demand. Trust your tastebuds. If you love this stall, great.
90 Whampoa Dr, #01-32, Singapore 320090

Herng Hao Chi Hokkien Mee
Revisited Herng Hao Chi just after a few days as I didn’t get enough of it the last time. Ordered my standard fare with additional ingredients etc. and waited about 20 mins. While picking up my plate, I was told that they forgot to give me additional eggs as I mentioned it in my last post. I am surprised that they quietly observed the reviews and took the opportunity to make good. I have no idea how they know it’s me as I didn’t introduce myself nor make it too obvious. Very observant and sincere action unlike some who would post a reply for everyone to see that you’re willing to compensate an egg. 
 huat ah.
Anyway, am convinced it’s a solid plate and consistent both times. Plenty of wok hei, robust broth, good texture and mix of noodles and thin bee hoon. Happy to see hardworking young entrepreneurs willing to do the heavy lifting these days. Keep it up.
Btw I walked by both Simon Road and Changi Village HKM stall at about 1245pm peak Saturday and both chefs were not frying. I think it’s hard for 3 HKM stalls to thrive in the same food center. At least one will go sooner or later and my best guess is CV as their HKM looks pretty sickly and pale.
Note that there is no Pork lard today (Sat 13th June).
Blk 210, Lor 8 Toa Payoh, #01-52, Singapore 310210

posts.author: Edwin Ng
posts.text:
Herng 好吃 Hokkien Mee
Lor 8 Toa Payoh, #01-52, Singapore 310210
Went there today at about 1pm. 5-10 min wait. Ordered $5 + $2 sotong and $2 prawns and 80 cent eggs. Total $9.80.
Not sure if eggs were added or forgotten but it’s ok if it was. No big deal. Portion was a little lesser than the typical Shiok given that I added prawns and sotong although I’d just say they are slightly more generous with the sotong. The stirred up pic looks small but I promise I didn’t take a bite. It was just stirred and I took the picture before I dug in. Taste wise, I would say it’s very much like an above average Shiok plate with pretty decent wok hei and prawn based stock. Probably slightly less salty than the avg Shiok plate. Reference to Shiok as the chef was apparently an ex Shiok chef.
One positive point was the pork lard as it is more airy and crispy than the avg Shiok pork lard.
Btw I’d like to point out something. If you do a review or plan to do one in the future, please don’t just state “no pork lard” because it does not add value. Is it “no pork lard” because you forgot to ask and when exactly was there no pork lard because sometimes people post a couple days later and complain “no pork lard” and best, they didn’t even request for it. That is really a disservice to the vendor as some may decide to go another day thinking that there is no pork lard for that day. Please, if you wanna post, then add value either by being factually accurate or don’t post at all.
I believe if individual chefs want to branch out after they get free training from Shiok or other bigger brand names, you must at the very least, replicate the dish. They can also have the flexibility to differentiate themselves either by tweaking the style or ingredients. If it’s going to be worse than the avg Shiok plate then you risk having close to no customers because they would rather go to the original (and plenty) Shiok branches.
I will revisit again since it’s not too far to have a second go at it after some time. Meanwhile, it isn’t bad as in over cooked or anything like that. It’s decent and doesn’t lose out to the avg Shiok plate. Let’s see if they can maintain or better, take it to the next level because more customers mean there is a direct impact to their P&L.

posts.author: Angeline Tan
posts.text:
Not all HKM are created equal….
After my post about Shiok HKM at Bishan, my aunt who saw it, called me this afternoon and “demanded” enthusiastically that I take her to eat HKM coz it looked so yummy. I decided to take her to Shiok at Beauty World as she lived nearer to that outlet. I thought all Shiok HKM are equal but..it seems that some are more equal than others. The verdict? My aunt was disappointed so was I, and sorely too! The $10 plate at this Beauty World seemed to be of the same size as the $6 plate at Bishan. The only difference is the $10 one has 6 prawns and a few more squid pieces with thicker pork belly slices; $6 plate has 3 prawns. Pork lard pieces seem to be more for the $6 plate though. Beauty World’s outlet needs to work on the frying — there’s no wokhei. The taste is lacklustre: no simmered prawn-tasting broth & the prawns though of good size, are really tasteless. They tasted like prawns which got thawed and just cooked for cooking sake, not for HKM sake! You could have seen my aunt’s face and her quietness after her first mouthful…
When I dropped her home, I apologised to her once more and promised to take her to the Shiok at Blk 504 Bishan St 11 #01-444.

posts.author: Geråld Heng
posts.text:
Decided to give FY HKM a second chance after my first visit to their original Tampines outlet, which left me with an overly sweet aftertaste.
This time, I visited their newer outlet at Blk 69 Bedok South.
First impressions were promising. The presentation was excellent, generously topped with pork lard. The prawns were fresh and succulent, while the sotong was decent. Most importantly, the sweetness that put me off during my first visit was no longer present.
Unfortunately, that’s where the positives ended.
While the pork lard was crispy, it lacked flavour and ended up tasting more like tiny fried crackers. The stock was also a letdown, carrying a distinct gamey note with an overwhelmingly seafood-forward profile that didn’t quite work for me.
Overall, the dish looked far better than it tasted. Although this second visit was an improvement over my first, it’s still not a bowl of hokkien mee that I’d find myself craving or making a special trip for. See less

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
I think this stall needs no introduction. Either you hate it or love it. For me, I’m neutral. 
So I actually was in the vicinity at Blk 58 to try one of the “hidden gem” BCM recommended by a certain YouTuber. Wah the BCM is solid, become one of my top 3. But portion a abit small, jiak buay pah. So I googled Hokkien Mee and out popped this stall which is like 2 blocks away. ON LAH!
Ordered the $6 plate, was given a buzzer and waited around 15 mins. Business seems good and got a lot of tapao orders. Also saw the boss walking around giving instructions. Haha.
Anyway, first glance, looks good. Smells good and portion size was about right. 3 small prawns, sotong and pork belly. Lard was given without asking. This is a gooey plate. 
First bite. Pepper. The broth was kinda peppery. Not sure if it was meant to be like this? Probably added too much pepper? Slowly I start to taste the mild wok hei and tasty prawny goodness. Prawns were small but fresh, sotong was nicely cooked and pork belly was tender. Lard was fresh, but not very crispy. Chilli was the belachan kind, nor my favourite but it’s ok. Chilli has a spicy kick which kinda elevated the peppery taste of the broth. i.e. made it taste more peppery. 
Overall it was a decent plate for me. $6 is pretty worth it. But as I was already 3/4 full from the BCM just 20 mins ago, I felt the portion was ok. Hungry folks probably need to top up noodles. See less
