posts.author: Icyflame Loh
posts.text:
Shiok Hokkien Mee (Jurong branch)
Block 130 Jurong Gateway Rd, #01-211, Singapore 600130
I had this hkm on 9 May 2026 for lunch at 11.55am. Didn't wanna write a review but they gave me free eggs add-on to do it lol... I don't think I will leave a Google review after this write up.
I am not sure if the person frying ain't on form or if the stars were not aligned on that day. The hkm tasted average at best but I have seen so many people raving about this new branch recently.
The presentation was decent from my pics. However, it is really a disappointing plate. Firstly, the prawns tasted funky.. They didn't seem not fresh but didn't taste good at all. The one other time I had lousy prawns in hkm were at Tun Xiang (Raffles Place branch).
Secondly, the add-on eggs seemed to be pre-fried for at least an hour already coz they were dry and cold. This was at noon and supposed to be peak hour.. Did they fry up a really big batch in the morning?
Thirdly, the pork lards were lao hong and tasteless. It failed to elevate the hkm.
Lastly and most importantly, the noodles... They were quite smoky and very oily. My wife could only finish half coz she didn't like it at all.
I really had high hopes for Shiok because so many had raved about them. I thought that their hkm can be somewhat similar to Youfu at Chinatown Complex which I could easily finish a $7 medium plate. Nevertheless, I hope improvements are already in place and they can continue to improve. Please let there be a decent thin bee hoon hkm in the West. Thanks!
For now, my go to in the West will be The Neighbourwok (Bukit Batok) and Feng.

Address: Block 618, Yishun Ring Road, Singapore 760618 
Every year during our birthday week, we love to give back to the community with a small donation. I have been doing this for more than 10 years and this year is the 4th time we've ordered from 618 Hokkien Mee. We ordered 100 packets of Fried Hokkien Mee, a local favourite that the elderly residents in Marsiling truly enjoy.
A big thank you to Boss Tran Lam for coming in 2 hours early to get everything ready. We also got to enjoy our own plate of FHM. The prawns today were especially big and succulent, absolutely delicious! Everything was neatly packed and ready for us to collect by 8.45am, thanks to her assistant. Their kindness and willingness to go the extra mile made this all possible, as we needed to collect our order and leave by 9am to arrive at Marsiling by 9.30am.
We are really glad that all 100 packets were delivered successfully, door to door, using the name list provided by Sun Love. It may be a small gesture, but we hope it brought a little warmth and joy to every elderly resident who received it. Giving back feels truly fulfilling, and we look forward to doing this again next year!
"Do not forget to do good and to share with others." — Hebrews 13:16 See less

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
If you hate to read, TL;DR: Wah, damn heng I ordered the $8 plate! Very good and gooey plate with awesome wok hei and flavours! Only thing is the ingredients (sotong and pork belly) cut kinda small.
Finally got the time to go food hunting and write. Was in the vicinity and finally had the chance to try this stall which I heard so much about. Was there during lunch time and almost every table has a plate of Hokkien Mee, which gives me high hopes. 
Ordered the $8 plate, given a buzzer and was informed there will be a bit of a wait. Lucky I had all the time in the world. Bought 2 spring rolls from the vegetarian stall and surprise! First bite of the spring roll and I was instantly transported back to my old army camp, Maju camp’s canteen the Malay stall couple. The spring rolls were nicely fried and super crispy with chunky mang kwang inside! Great value for $1.20
Anyway, after 15 mins wait, buzzer rang, chiong ahhh!!! First glance, everything looks right. Asked for more lard, and they happily obliged with 2 more spoonfuls! Smells awesome and packed with ingredients albeit cut in small pieces. 4 small prawns, thinly sliced pork belly and sotong. Chilli looks fiery and makes me sweat by just looking at it. This is more of a wet style HKM. 
First spoonful. Holy Hokkien Mee.. wok hei hits you. Flavours were all there. Noodles nicely done, not mushy. Gooey and super yummy. Prawns are fresh, sotong and pork cooked just nice, but cut kinda small pieces. Pork lard was good, no rancid smell, fresh but not very crispy. Chilli as I guessed was fiery hot, make me sweat. I finished the plate in less than 10 mins. Sibei Heng I ordered $8. 
Overall, this is a really good and satisfying plate. A close competitor of my favourite You Fu. Best thing is that they are fairly near to me, and lagi best is I’ll be moving to the BTO beside the coffeeshop in 1-2 years. Hopefully they will still be there by then as the coffeeshop has quite a few empty stalls, which probably indicates high turnover. Next stall to try is 99 at the nearby hawker, which I know there are some bad reviews. 
 See less

posts.text:
Had to try 69 Hokkien Mee since a lot of people say this was good. I’ve already tried Fung Yi outlet here already so I’m here to compare.
What I liked about it:
I can see why 69 Hokkien Mee has a lot of fans for sure! Their sotong is perfectly cooked. Their pork lard also is one of the best I’ve had! Very clean tasting and crisp! Not too hard as well. It doesn’t have that over sweetness which is good too. The chilli is the belacan type that I love and not the sweet Nasi Lemak sambal kind that I dislike (I’m looking at you Swee Guan 
)
What I didn’t like about it:
It is VERY VERY WET. For those who prefer their Hokkien Mee wet then this is definitely for you. I’m not a super huge fan of super wet kinds like this but it’s not a deal breaker for me. It’s almost porridge-like. The noodles were super soft leaving almost no chew. I could almost drink it up whole. Not unpleasant, just weird.
Overall not a bad Hokkien Mee but it’s made for a very specific group of people I feel. 
With that, I’m leaning slightly more towards Fung Yi

Second visit to Herng 好吃, this time during peak dinner hour. Had originally planned to visit Hock Kee, but they'd already closed before 8pm, so ended up here at the food centre instead. Good news this time, I managed to get a fresh batch, so the noodles were properly done with no sogginess, unlike my first visit. The chilli is undeniably the soul of this dish. Unfortunately, the wok-hey wasn't quite there today and there were quite a few charred bits, a telltale sign that the wok wasn't being cleaned between each batch. Honestly for me, this is an average plate of FHM. I don't quite see how it justifies the hype it's been getting. Everytime I go to Geylang Bahru, I can always kill 2 birds with 1 stone - my favourite chicken rice (which I shall gatekeep, though if you know the hawker centre its not difficult to guess which one) and Ah Ong Hokkien Mee. And today's box was absolutely stunning. Strong wok hei is not his calling card, though it certainly tastes well fried. Rather, it is how the dish comes together as a symphony - deep prawny umami, generous fresh ingredients, coated with a stock that has reduced to the texture of creamy carbonara, studded with pork lard and fried egg bits with a good hit of fried garlic. And I noticed that he has worked on his chilli - its now a fullblown sambal belacan, which works perfectly. The spice is definitely there, but it works to enhance rather than overpower the dish and the heady belacan umami adds another string to the flavour bow. I feel like every successive serving I've had has only gotten better and better.

All this for just $5 a serving (add 20c for takeaway). This is hawker food at its best - world class in flavour, utterly affordable in pricing. Not many hawkers are able to (or want to) achieve this - honestly the sacrifices may not be worth it for everyone depending on their situation. And neither should we demand it - hawker food just needs to meet basic needs. But when a hawker aspires towards and achieves this, he deserves all the plaudits in the world. Thank you Ah Ong!

comments.text:
2w Bad experience (Food so so only).
We ordered two plates of HKM to eat there, but when our number was called, the food had been packed into two takeaway containers instead. We were actually seated right in front of the stall.
洪志忠 collected the food and brought the two containers back to our table. I asked him, “Aren’t we supposed to be eating here?” He just replied, “Never mind.” I then asked if the stall had charged us for the takeaway containers. He said he wasn’t sure, and when I asked how much we had paid, he said he didn’t know.
As I was already very hungry, I didn’t go to the stall immediately. I waited until the queue had dispersed before approaching the lady who was taking the orders.
I told her, “We were supposed to be dining in, but you packed our food into takeaway containers.”
She immediately replied, “Sorry, it was a mistake.”
I then asked, “Did you charge us for the containers?”
Without hesitation, she said, “I’ll refund you 60 cents now,” and returned the money.
This made me wonder: if I hadn’t gone back to ask, would the stall have simply kept the extra 60 cents, even though the mistake was theirs? If it was genuinely an honest mistake, they should have refunded the container charge as soon as the food was handed to us, instead of waiting until I questioned them. HKM Fix at Bugis Fish Head – Kelantan Lane! 
Dropped by Bugis Fish Head at Kelantan Lane today and had their Hokkien Mee (HKM). Nicely wok-fried yellow noodles with thin bee hoon, loaded with pork slices, squid, egg all coated in a rich, savoury prawn stock. The sambal gave it a nice spicy kick, pork lard crackling was crispy and airy
6$ / plate
Simple, comforting, and satisfying. Definitely worth a stop if you’re around the area and craving a good plate of Hokkien Mee.
In addition to HKM they offer many other dishes that I’ll definitely come to try !
 Bugis Fish Head
Kelantan Lane, Singapore

posts.author: AhJie Hokkien Mee
posts.text:
AHJIE HOKKIEN MEE IS THE BEST DAMN HOKKIEN MEE ANG MO KIO HAS EVER SEEN (to me lah)
just want to shoutout one of my favourite HKM stalls. it’s not my number 1 but it’s definitely one of my favourites. i have it at least once a week, sometimes 2-3 since i live nearby.
objectively the wok hei is SPOT ON, and every mouthful is packed with umami. my only feedback is that their pork belly is a little tougher compared to other stalls. they can also be slightly stingy with the pork lard sometimes but if you buay paiseh and ask for more they’re quite nice and will oblige unless they’re really running low. but if you go for late dinner and they run out of pork lard then no choice lor no pork lard

posts.text:
Umami Hokkien mee @709 Geylang Rd.
Was there 5 mins before they opened at 12 noon. 5 people in the queue before me and about 10 mins wait. 2 young men handling the stall.
2 medium prawns that were reasonably fresh, 5 slivers of sotong and maybe 5 thin pieces of pork belly in a small plate for $6. I asked for some pork lard but they were very ordinary tasting. Chilli was nondescript in flavour and nothing to rave about. The hkm is the semi wet type. Did not detect any wokhei, but some sweetish type of umami. Towards the end of the plate, it became obvious where the umami came from. MSG.
Loads of it. I had a bad thirst for the next few hours.
Rather disappointing. 618 and Ah Huat would beat it hands down. 5/10.

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
Battle of the Titans at Hougang 105.
TL;DR - Personally I prefer QJ over BS. QJ is more value for money with more ingredients, bigger prawns, fresher lard and overall tastier noodles. The only saving grace for BS is their chilli. 
Review proper: 
Today is Friday, since got some time, so decided to go eat Hokkien Mee. Just a 5 min drive from my place, surprisingly this is my first time trying both. And my first time to hoot 2 plates which was damn filling.. cannot imagine that Zermatt Neo 
Was there at about 1.45pm and decided to start off with BS. Uncle seemed a bit stunned that so late still got people order. First glance, serving looked kinda small for $5, and seems to have a lot of vegetables (green onions and bean sprouts). Lard was given without asking. Taste wise, kinda lacking wok hei and umami. I could only taste a very raw vegetable taste, if you know what I mean. Ingredients (sotong and pork belly) were fresh and well cooked. Lard was fresh, but not very crispy. 3 prawns (1 without tail)  but very small, like those “standard” prawns you find in your usual Hor Fun. Their only saving grace was their chilli. It had this smoky flavour and pairs well with the noodles. Overall, I was kinda disappointed as I had high hopes for this stall since I heard so much about them. 
Next up, QJ. Ordered a $5 plate too. This uncle seemed more friendly. Haha. Let’s hope his HKM is good. Had to wait about 8 mins for my plate as uncle was frying a new batch. First glance, normal looking plate, but I can see a lot of ingredients. Confirm more value for money for the same $5. Lard was also free flow, I scooped as much as I wanted! First bite. Confirm way better than the previous plate I devoured 10 mins ago. Hint of wok hei and pretty good and strong umami taste! Lard was crispy and fresh and CHUNKY! Holy lard-tastic! The best part was the plate was packed with chunky ingredients! Sotong was slightly overcooked but still ok, pork belly was chunky and tender. Though only 2 prawns, but they are big and very fresh, and definitely not the “standard” prawns you find in your usual Hor Fun. This plate was so good that I totally forgot about the chilli till I was halfway thru the plate. Anyway, the chilli was pretty standard and one dimensional (just flat out spicy). Honestly, you don’t need the chill at all. 
Overall, I personally prefer QJ over BS because of value for money (amount of ingredients and type of prawns) and overall better tasting noodles and lard. If only I could eat QJ HKM with BS chilli… haha! 
Lastly, I know there are fans of both stalls, and this review is just my personal preference and opinions. See less

posts.text:
Shiok Hokkien Mee @ Serangoon
Since it’s the nearest outlet, I decided to give this branch a try.
When ordering, I saw those dishes being served and they looked like it has been sitting around for a while - broth soaked in and slightly stiff. Hoping that a fresh new batch would be different. This was around 12 noon. I waited 15 mins and the look of it wasn’t much better.
- hardly any bee hoon. Mostly noodles. Texture was soggy.
- Little to no wok hei
- Some of the prawns looked bruised and wasn’t as firm as the usual.
- much less umami than usual. Not Shiok.
- I ordered $6 + $4 ingredients and egg. You can see the receipt states + $2 ingredients +$2 prawns but I think it is because the cashier didn’t seem to know how to do a 2 x ingredients. You can see that there is hardly any sotong. I took out the prawns and separated them and took another picture so it’s not like I deliberately hid the sotong. Not much pork either.
Overall, quite disappointed as my weekly HKM quota has been used for a very average plate of HKM. Probably will not visit this branch again even though it’s the nearest to me.

posts.text:
Shiok’s 9th & latest outlet - Serangoon!
Popped by Shiok’s latest outlet opening today!
Thrilled to see the whole OG team again out in (almost) full force.
I still recall their early Youfu Golden Mile days.
Along the line of conventional hawker stalls of 2F Golden Mile Hawker, was the early Shiok hidden by the corner, fka YouFu, where there was a group of trio attending to the wok, and blasting EDMs & techno music while raving to the rhythm of the wok, dishing out our flavorful Hokkien mee.
What made me try em out was just because, “dude they were so cool???”
Fast forward to today, these EDM wok-raving HKM guys have now taken a conventional dish, so representative of Singaporean Hawker Culture, and scaled it to a whole network islandwide, easily recognizable.
Surely there were incidents of imperfections, but these guys were also never one to hide behind the screens. Humble and honest, always taking in feedback to improve wherever possible. & the results show - a good base reference taste no matter where you go, chili still packs a damn punch, ingredients continue to be fresh & no more “running out of xyz” anymore.
Some of us might have noticed they also now have even their first case of early employees branching out - & I liken this to the potential scenario of a PayPal Mafia forming. Surely it is quite a stretch for this comparison at this stage. However, they sure damn deserve some congratulations and celebration for all the success they have achieved, walking the path less travelled.
Mitch & team, congratulations, happy for you, happy for the future of Hokkien Mee!

Address: Block 323 Bukit Batok Street 33, Singapore 650323
Tried Mian Wang 1971 today. The prawns, sotong and pork belly were all good. Solid prawn stock and nice wok-hey, you can taste the effort. The sambal belacan was too spicy. I understand that some people like it spicy, but when the sambal belacan is blasting that much heat, it actually works against the dish. You lose the sweetness of the prawn stock and the wok-hey flavour gets buried under all that spice. The pork lard also burnt, not the golden brown crispy kind. Honestly this shouldn't even be served to customers. Burnt lard just spoils the whole dish, no matter how good the rest is. Sambal belacan should complement the FHM, not overpower it. A good chilli enhances the dish without drowning out what's already good about the ingredients. Hope they can tune down the spiciness a little and get that lard crisping just right. This stall clearly has the fundamentals, just need to fine-tune the balance. See less

[BEDOK CORNER, LATE 1960s] 

This photo by Janet Brannigan takes us straight back. 

A pioneer hawker at Bedok Corner, Singapore's famous open-air seaside food spot in the East. White singlet, shorts, big wok over fire. No hood, no aircon, just skill and wok hei. 

You can see it all:
• The dish: 
Likely Fried Hokkien Mee sizzling in the wok 
• The setup:
Wooden multi-tiered counter with small bowls of ingredients, fresh eggs, tomatoes, and bottles of Del Monte ketchup + chili sauce 
• The era:
Before street vendors were moved into indoor hawker centres. This was roadside dining at its rawest and best 

This was how our food culture started. Sweat, heat, and heart. 
Uncles like this fed generations of Singaporeans after work, after school, after a swim at the beach. 

Bedok Corner is gone now, but the memory of that smoky air, the sound of the ladle hitting the wok, and the taste of that first bite... it stays with us. 

To all the pioneer hawkers: thank you  You built the foundation of Singapore's hawker heritage.

posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
Saw someone else posted this newly opened HKM stall near my office, today fast hand fast leg go down try liao.
TL;DR - This is a pretty good plate for me! Not much wok hei, but really good and balanced umami flavours. Big prawns were fresh and crunchy. Pork (pulled not sliced) was chunky and tender. The chilli for me is definitely home made and unique. It’s not spicy, and it’s not sambal or belacan. I can’t really describe it but it has this sourish curry/masala taste which goes well with the noodles!
Review proper:
Lunch time liao! Took a train to Hong Lim just to try this stall which looked so promising in the pics of someone who posted. Reached around 1pm. Was 3rd in line and they just finished frying a new batch.
They have either normal plate ($5 onwards) or big prawns plate (min $8). I opted for the big prawns $9. Got my order within like 5 mins.
First glance, super promising. I’m excited sia. Condiments were self service and free flow, no lard though. Portion looks huge also. Mild wok hei aroma and came with 3 big prawns, pork and lots of egg. No sotong though.. The pork don’t look like usual sliced pork belly. Instead it seems to be pull pork which looked super tender. This was a gooey and not so soupy plate. 
Mandatory lime in and first bite. Wow.. mild wok hei and the umami flavours were super balanced! Nice surprise! Tried the pork, super tender and chunky. Prawns were also super big and fresh with a crunchy bite. After just a few bites, I was already telling myself, this one $9 worth it! 
One thing to note is the bee hoon. It has a good bite to it. Probably because they use dried thick bee hoon instead of thin. So it’s in between thin and fresh thick bee hoon. 
Next, the chilli. The chilli is surely home made. It doesn’t look like the usual sambal or fiery red belacan. I was expecting it to give a good kick, so I just mixed a bit into the noodles. No kick at all. The chilli wasn’t spicy at all. It also has a unique taste which I can’t really describe, but it has a bit of that Indian curry/masala taste. Though not spicy, I kinda like the chilli. It pairs really well with the noodles and cuts thru the richness like butter. Really unique chilli! 
Overall, this was a pretty good plate for me. Not the very best of the best, but it’s good enough for me to drop by occasionally to eat. I’ll just come here for the chilli. Haha! See less
+2

posts.text:
I went to Chomp Chomp today, looking forward to my favourite plate of Hokkien mee.
When I saw the stall closed, I asked the neighbouring hawker if Uncle was okay.
They quietly told me he had passed away.
My heart sank.
Ah Hock Fried Hokkien Mee wasn’t just another hawker stall to me. I grew up eating his Hokkien mee, and over the years it became the Hokkien mee I would always crave for. 
Uncle was never loud or showy. He always had a quiet smile for his customers, then turned back to his wok with complete focus. You could see the passion he had for his craft in every plate he fried.
In a city where hawker food is part of who we are, people like Uncle are more than cooks. They are custodians of traditions, memories, and flavours that become woven into our lives.
Rest in peace, Uncle.
Thank you for the countless plates of Hokkien mee, for the dedication you poured into every wok, and for leaving behind a legacy that so many of us will remember and miss.
I also hope his sons, who have been by his side at the stall for many years, will continue the craft and keep his legacy alive. It would be a fitting tribute to a lifetime spent behind the wok.
My deepest condolences to his family.
If you have memories of Uncle or his Hokkien mee, I hope you’ll share them in the comments. I think his family would find comfort in knowing how many lives he touched through something as simple, yet as special, as a plate of Hokkien mee.
Photos: Google, shared in remembrance. See less

Every time I come back from overseas, I will visit this store, because I like the balance of too wet or too dry version of Hokkien noodles with slim bee hoon & yellow noodles. The umami is thick with prawn head garlic, pork, bone flavour. And they usually give two lime for my order of $8 and six fresh prawns, which taste very crunchy. There are also slices of pork belly, subtly slice with good “wok hei” And not overpowering infuse to create stickiness in the soup, and that’s a some bit of collagen. This is one of the better local Hokkien fried prawn noodles which are highly recommend. Generous serving albeit missing squid, for those who like more solid seafood. That taste is excellent. 4.7/5 my score See less

However the Lard though crispy but it is rancid. I did not finish the plate. My fault as I mixed the rancid lard spoiled the taste. Right pic is 777 Google scored lower. But it is fair. Prawn not as fresh. Same like YH. No wok hei. Slightly better broth and taste better. Lard better. Crispy, not rancid. Chilli decent. Overall is decent with a plus. I will still come as some days I don't need heavy taste. I will prefer 777 in taste. YH for its fresh ingredient With NBwok just 5 mins walk. NB definitely worth the travel. In Bukit Batok my preference NBWok/Born. Tie but I go Born for extra lard AhHuat/MianWang. AH my preferred. MW for varieties. Thanks all folks. P.S negative comments not needed here. posts.author: Andy Quek
posts.text:
Finally came back to this 431 Hokkien Mee after coming here that day to find it closed. TL;DR - Very little hint of wok hei, bland noodles and almost tasteless broth. Chilli elevated it a bit, but not enough. And for $7 for a small plate, sorry but I’ll pass. So I’m back here at 431 Hokkien Mee after coming here last week only to find it closed. Arrived at about 5pm, no customers. Auntie, likely a PRC, smiled happily at me machiam was I was the first customer of the day. Ask if the smallest was $7 and she said yes, ok so let’s try. For $7 a plate, better be good. Given a buzzer and waited for about 5-6 minutes. At least it’s freshly fried and not reheated noodles. Buzzer rang and I went to collect my noodles, first glance, serving was bigger than usual, kind soupy, and I saw small prawns which were butterflied, sotong, big chunks of egg, and chunky pork lard bits on top! Chilli was the normal sambal, and it was free flow self service together with the lime. If only the lard was free flow… haha! Sat down and took a whiff. Can smell some wok hei, promising. Squeezed the lime, quick mix and first bite - slight taste of wok hei. That’s all. Nothing else. I tasted another bite, boy the noodles were bland. Maybe she forget to add fish sauce? Tasted a spoonful of broth, wah also bland… give it another good mix and tasted again, confirm bland and almost tasteless. Disappointed. Mixed in some chilli to try, it did elevated the dish a bit but sadly, not enough. On the bright side, the serving was pretty generous, and there were heaps of sotong which was cooked really well. Prawns fresh but rather small and were butterflied for some reason, plating maybe? The pork lard was also decent, still crispy. No pork belly though. Overall, this didn’t hit the mark for me. It felt like a poorly done wet bee hoon from a zi char stall. Especially when it’s $7 a plate, I was expecting more! Maybe bigger and better prawns? And maybe auntie did really forgot to add fish sauce? But the seasoning for the broth was really lacking. Lastly, what really irked me was the huge chunks of garlic (last picture) which they didn’t even bother to mince properly. Reminds me of China cooking at the Mala stall with huge chunks of garlic. Probably will not come back anymore for this. 😅

comments.author: Louis Chan
comments.text:
2w Ah Yu
Broth - Umami and robust.
Prawns - Sweet and succulent.
Noodles - Ratio of thin bee hoon and noodles almost equal, my personal preference is to have slightly lesser bee hoon. Wok hei is present, not at Ah Jie, Shiok or Herng levels but pretty good.
Overall taste: Clean tasting, not heavy on the palate. The two limes are given by default, helps cut through the dish and bring balance. I would give a 7.8 rating, very satisfying plate.
Geylang Lor 29
Broth - Umami and robust.
Prawns - Tasted like farmed prawns but fresh.
Noodles - More on the heavier side, stronger alkaline taste. Bee hoon and yellow noodle ratio just nice. Stronger wok hei, however bean sprouts maybe a little undercooked which mars the overall taste.
Overall taste: Those with a heavy palate or seeking for a nostalgic taste would like this. Could taste the fragrance of peanuts hence it is likely that peanut oil was used which lends a very nice aroma evoking the old school vibes. It’s a good plate with fat pieces of sotong, something you hardly find these days. Ah Yu Broth - Umami and robust. Prawns - Sweet and succulent. I went to 660A Edgedale Plain coffee shop to try out the Hong Xing handmade fish ball when I read there's a branch nearby my place. In the same coffee shop, there's a Fried Hokkien Mee that caught my eye. The cook has similar built as BFB hokkien mee, so naturally it trigger my instincts to try. Taste, I say it is very flavorful. Chili kick is just nice for me. Taste profile reminds me of Ah Ong. Only complaint is they are not selling it at $5 as that is making their western food even more value for money for their high protein ratio.

posts.author: Eric Widjaja
posts.text:
@I have always been a avid fan of Shiok, they are the reason why I change my love for HKM from thick beehoon to thin beehoon. This time round , they have upped their game to another level. This move to open till 1230am is like the best thing that can happen. I work shifts , and I end work most of the time around 2300hrs, just about enough time to travel down to this serangoon outlet to order a plate of wholesome goodness. Shiok Hokkien Mee staff has this never ending bursting energy that never failed to put a smile on their customers. I was greeted with smiles and energy even when I arrive at around 2330hrs. They told me "boss, we have run out of sotong and pork belly, apologies." I said no worries and ordered two plates for me and my wife. Within 15 mins the buzzer rang and here comes two plate of wonderful-looking HKM that totally entices our taste buds. Just look at the effort they did to make up for the loss of sotong and pork belly, to me, this is the sincerity of the team. We truly cherish it and finished every last bit of it. Thoroughly enjoyed , the umami, the fantastic chilli, the noodles and the freshness of the big prawns. What more can I ask for ? Heartfelt thanks to Mitchell and team for bringing this to our local folks.

Been in this group long enough but only reading the recommendations on my armchair, not many post-worthy HKM vendors around the South-West region for me to rara about until I stumbled upon this 
For all the HKM fanatics residing around/near Clementi, don't waste your time with the nearby EatBar or free-egg-for-review options elsewhere 
Here is my 
1) Non-AI written
2) Non-Sponsored 
Virgin post in this group 
Set foot at 378 Clementi (whose coffeeshop is, dare I say, the most quiet and secluded amongst all the competitors in the entire estate) few weeks back and noticed a stall aptly named "Hokkien Mee" - no fanciful gimmicks which is just what we love, isn't it
Simple signboard - $6/$8/$10 option, 
Chilli or don't want chilli 
A $6 plate is more than enough to fill your stomach
First trip - I was blown away by the wokhei, aroma and portions but prawns were mushy
Second trip - Broth was too salty for me, but prawns were fresh 
Third time today - The best i had so far, everything on point 
Three times, three different guys at the wok

So here I am at last, at Big Fat Boy Hokkien Mee. First off, they are friendly and they can customize your FHM whether you want it dryish or wettish😉. I just went with whatever his norm was. posts.text:
Ho Ji Fried Hokkien Mee Noodles
Mayflower market and food center
Was in the area trying out hup kee fishball noodles and thought about giving this a shot since I'm seldom in the area.
Going in this review blind and ordered the smallest option $5 as I'm full from breakfast. Quite a sizable amount was plated and will fill the avg person up unlike some small options from other stalls. Cough cough, Tian Seng and Hainan I'm name dropping you two lol. Downside will be the glaring lack of chives and sotong. Prawns were probably harvested from the kindergarden and tasted of a monastic life lived (bland). Bearing in mind it's $5, so please manage your expectations in this economy.
Broth was the glue that bound everything together and saved this dish. There is a pleasant smokiness that lends depth on top of a nice savory forward stock. Was pleasantly delighted by it however maybe can braise the noodles abit longer as the bee hoon haven't fully absorb the goodness.
Chilli was sour/spicy and the acidity lent a good kick to brighten up the dish. Would suggest tasting it before mixing it in if you are spice adverse.
I would eat it again if craving hkm in the area but the fishball noodle was better use of calories.
Jeremy

Downside will be the glaring lack of chives and sotong. Prawns were probably harvested from the kindergarden and tasted of a monastic life lived (bland). Bearing in mind it's $5, so please manage your expectations in this economy. 

Broth was the glue that bound everything together and saved this dish. There is a pleasant smokiness that lends depth on top of a nice savory forward stock. Was pleasantly delighted by it however maybe can braise the noodles abit longer as the bee hoon haven't fully absorb the goodness.

Chilli was sour/spicy and the acidity lent a good kick to brighten up the dish. Would suggest tasting it before mixing it in if you are spice adverse. 

I would eat it again if craving hkm in the area but the fishball noodle was better use of calories.

posts.text:
Two food variety shows don’t like Chuan FHKM
wa recently got 2 food variety shows on youtube go around hunt for hokkien mee to review. then when both groups reach Chuan, you can tell they trying not to offend people and trying to find other nice things to say. probably scared kena from siao lang in this group
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1zHTzkW285o
https://youtu.be/-nVnXqs3xpY?is=GLO_5Nl8PZl0Y1Vy
but not surprised they were this way as Chuan FKHM was such a disappointing experience especially since there’s so much hype when i went to try.
Wok Hei: 8/10 — fry the wok hei until can smell from first floor make you damn hungry and excited
Flavour: -3/10 — walau but then when you eat it you’re like what the heck. it’s completely flavourless except for alkaline taste from the huang mian.
Ingredients: 8/10 — super fresh ingredients. highlight is the thick uniformly sliced chunks of pork belly which are qq and v succulent. good thing about no flavour is that you can taste the ingredients natural subtle taste.. if you’re into that but the star of HKM should be the noodles.
Pork Lard: 9/10 — super airy and crispy unlike other stalls sometimes feel like biting into rock
portion is good, chilli is spicy but ok ok lor? texture is sticky and dry which is fine but combined with the flavour (or lack thereof) made it a struggle to eat. must tell yourself try not to waste food lor. i waited 30mins and you can see from my photo there’s a thick clump of beehoon which tells me they didn’t really mix/fry properly.
will i go back even if im nearby? definitely not. and i dont think the hosts of these 2 shows will either. would rather eat maggi goreng from the mamak.
how about you? what do you think! be honest!!

posts.text:
After the recent saga of being sabotaged by phantom 1 star google reviews, I decided to drop by today to give some support.
TL;DR - To me, this HKM the flavors are on point, though lacking in wok hei. For $9 a plate, serving size looks kinda small, but size isn’t everything, in the noodles are lots of ingredients. Sotong, pork belly, and medium-big prawns which are really fresh and crunchy. Lard bits and chili were also up to standard. Overall it’s an above average plate for me!
Review proper:
So decided to go the lagoon hawker centre today because I wanted my favorite Ah Hwee chicken wings. At the same time also go support this HKM stall who recently posted they go sabotaged by phantom 1 star google reviews. 
Went around 6+, entire hawker centre was pretty quiet for a Friday evening. Ordered the $9 plate and managed to have a chat with the boss Kid Chua. Glad to hear that google managed to remove those phantom reviews already. Was given a buzzer and waited for around 15 mins I guess.
Moment my buzzer beeped, I left my place at the chicken wing stall to collect my HKM first. Chicken wing can wait. HKM cannot wait… haha. First glance, serving was kinda small for $9, but later then I will find out that size isn’t everything. It was also slightly wet, but slowly drying up. Looks promising, I was telling myself in my mind…
Sat down, lime in, and took a whiff. Not much wok hei. Dug around and saw like 4 med-big prawns. Best part is it was loaded with chunky pork belly and sotong. First bite, wow! Nice flavors and good umami! Not much wok hei unfortunately. Tasted a piece of pork lard. Nice and crispy, no rancid oil smell. Got add salt one. GOOD!. I WISH more lard was given though. Put down my chopsticks and went to wait for my chicken wings.
After a good 10 min wait, finally came back with the wings. Guess what? WISH granted! I saw a small plate with extra pork lard!!! Missus told me that the HKM guy came over and offered the extra lard. What a nice gesture! Continued eating my hokkien mee. Boy it was good now that it soaked up all the gooey goodness. Highlight for me was definitely the prawns! Medium-big size, nice and crunchy! Tasted the chili, it was good too. Tangy and spicy, and surprised that it didn’t overpower the goodness of the noodles.
Overall, this was a very good plate for me. Definitely in my top 5. Definitely would come back for Hokkien mee next time, not for the chicken wings. Haha.
P.S. After the plate of hokkien met, I still hoot 6 wings. Standard of the wings were as good as ever. Only thing I hate is the messy queue system which seems to be all over the place. The mess can easily be solved by giving our queue numbers. See less

posts.author: Tang Ji Li
posts.text:
Went to Geylang area to try SG UMAMI, ordered the $8 portion. Ordered around 6.30pm and received my order within 10 minutes. The umami taste of the stock was pretty good, 3 large fresh prawns, soft sotong rings and pork belly was given. The thin bee hoon absorbed the flavours very well. I like the added chives, provides colour while garnishing the HKM. 2 types of chilli was provided, sambal chilli which tasted kinda sweet and the other more citrusy/sour chilli. Would come back and try again if I am in the area.
Location 
: 709 Geylang Rd, Singapore 389624
Edit: Added chives, not spring onions.

Shiok @ Serangoon Central (Broadway coffeeshop, Blk 261).
$6 (small) and $8 (medium) for dine-in, plus one small for takeaway.

Hokkien Mee Review
Tried the Hokkien mee here and honestly really enjoyed it! The noodles had a nice wok hei and the flavour was savoury without being too overwhelming. The prawns and ingredients tasted fresh, and the texture of the noodles was just right. Portion was decent too.
Overall, a really satisfying plate of Hokkien mee and definitely something I’d order again.

posts.author: Gopalsamy Rajkumar
posts.text:
Address: Block 80 Circuit Road, #02-05, Singapore 370080
Despite the recent low rating from some KOLs, the crowd coming to Chuan remains as strong as before. I waited patiently for slightly over an hour for my lunch today, and honestly, the experience was still as good as before.
The boss remains quite consistent with his cooking.
Taste is subjective. What one person dislikes doesn’t mean everyone will dislike it, just as what one person loves doesn’t mean everyone will love it.
A KOL giving a low rating doesn’t automatically mean the food is bad or that people will stop coming. In fact, the customers today seemed to say otherwise.
And honestly, if someone too used to swallow the food, can we really say he has properly tasted and experienced it? At the end of the day, don't just follow someone else's rating. Try it yourself and decide. See less
